articles.title: Moral Maze - How should we respond to rising mental distress? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Live debate examining the moral issues behind one of the week's news stories.
articles.body: A record one in seven people in England were prescribed antidepressants in the last year, according to NHS figures. More than nine million patients now take the drugs, and while they may be essential in many cases, the prevalence of mental ill-health – stress, anxiety, burnout – is a moral issue as well as a medical one. Why are more people, including under-18s, presenting to their GP with these conditions, and what should we do about it? Many clinicians believe anti-depressants serve an important function, including in milder cases, particularly where access to talking therapies is limited. This, they say, is both a practical and compassionate response to suffering, and a respect for patient autonomy. However, there is disagreement among psychiatrists, some of whom argue that everyday stress is being patholigised. They see drugs as morally hazardous in certain cases, since they alter mental sates, blunt emotions and create dependence on the drugs themselves, reducing people’s long-term capacity to cope. Beyond the clinical response, there are deeper questions to consider about our society and culture. NHS figures suggest patients in the most deprived areas were prescribed antidepressants 44% more than in the least deprived areas. Many mental health campaigners see the crisis as a social harm, caused by poverty, inequality and insecurity. They believe that rather than simply treating the symptoms of distress, we have a social responsibility to fix the structural causes: better housing, secure working conditions, and a fairer distribution of the resources people need to live dignified lives. For others, the crisis represents something even more fundamental: a loss of meaning, purpose, connection, and resilience. How should we respond to rising mental distress? Chair: Michael Buerk Panel: Ash Sarkar, Giles Fraser, Anne McElvoy and Carmody Grey Witnesses: Ellie Cannon, Joanna Moncrieff, Polly Mackenzie and Mark Vernon Producer: Dan Tierney Assistant producer: Peter Everett Editor: Tim Pemberton

The Bayeux Tapestry exhibition is going to be open to the public at the British Museum in London from 10 September.

The 70m (230ft) tapestry, originally embroidered in England but kept for centuries in France, tells the story of the Norman Conquest and the Battle of Hastings in 1066.

Sending the tapestry to the British Museum had been announced by Macron during the French state visit to the UK in July 2025, as an emblem of the strong partnership between the countries.

And you don’t have to go to a fancy department store or niche boutique to find one. How I picked the best bath towels from Amazon To narrow down key features to look for in bath towels, I spoke to interior designers and a design expert from Brooklinen. A lower GSM (under 400) indicates a lighter, thinner weight towel, while a towel with a higher GSM tends to be thicker and fluffier — making it more absorbent. articles.title: Are Screen Protectors Still Worth Buying? | NBC Selected
articles.summary: The best screen protectors can shield your phone from scratches, cracks or even shattering. We spoke with repair experts about how they work and the best ones to buy
articles.body: If cracking your phone screen ranks near the top of your list when it comes to tech disasters, you’re not alone. It is one of the reasons there are so many different types of screen protectors available. I consider myself very kind to my gadgets — I take good care of them and don’t needlessly throw them around or put them somewhere they’ll get banged up. But even I drop my phone a couple of times a week. Every time I do, I worry I’ll pick it up and find my screen cracked or scratched. Thankfully, between my phone case and screen protector, I haven’t had that happen in more than a decade. According to tech repair experts I spoke with, if you pick the right screen protector and install it correctly it will provide extra protection for pricey gadgets. Below, these experts explain how screen protectors work and how to select the right one for your needs, plus they share their personal recommendations for anyone looking for the best screen protector for a new device. Want more from NBC Select? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best screen protectors of 2026 The recommendations below come directly from our experts or NBC Selected staff, and are largely products with thousands of positive customer reviews online. Best overall Experts I spoke with recommend Spigen as a great brand for most people. Arthur Zilberman, president of laptop repair company Laptop MD, says this model is case-friendly, affordable and durable. It’s also easy to install — it comes with an alignment tray that you place on top of your phone screen and press down on to secure the protector in place. You get two screen protectors with each purchase, in case you ever need to replace the first one. This screen protector is available for iPhone (linked above), Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel devices. Runner-up Mac Frederick, the owner of Phone Repair Philly, says Zagg screen protectors are a great value for the quality you get. The XTR4 version is the brand’s strongest model, made with tempered glass that’s reinforced with graphene, making it much stronger, according to the brand. It comes with an installation tray that helps align your phone and avoid air bubbles as you apply it. This screen protector is available for iPhone (linked above) and Samsung Galaxy devices, among others. Best budget For affordable durability, Frederick recommends Supershieldz tempered glass screen protectors. This set comes with three tempered glass screen protectors, each with rounded edges and a fingerprint-resistant coating, according to the brand. Supershieldz’s tempered glass screen protectors are available for devices from Apple, Samsung, Google and LG. Best for camera lenses and tablets Zilberman recommends Ailun as another budget screen protector brand. Similar to Supershieldz, this three-pack of screen protectors has a fingerprint-resistant coating, but it also comes with an installation frame in the box that shoppers say make applying the protectors easier. The pack of screen protectors also comes with several camera lens protectors so you can prevent scratches there too. Ailun screen protectors are available for iPhone (linked above), Samsung devices and iPads. Best privacy screen protector This screen protector makes it harder for onlookers to see what is on your iPhone screen — it looks totally dark if you look at it from the sides. As with any privacy protector, it makes your screen’s colors and brightness appear a bit faded compared to using a regular screen protector. Shoppers say they’ve dropped their phones on hardwood, tile and concrete without the screen cracking. Staff pick NBC Selected reporters Ashley Morris and Zoe Malin both use this screen protector. Morris has been using Otterbox’s Premium Blue Light protectors for years and finds them very durable and easy to install. As someone who drops their phone a lot (as in multiple times a day), her protectors tend to get a bit banged up over time, so she also loves that Otterbox’s warranty program lets her replace the protector for free (excluding shipping). Are screen protectors still worth it ? If you tend to drop your phone or simply want peace of mind when it comes to protecting expensive products, a screen protector may be a smart investment. Plus, scratching or damaging your screen is easier than you may think. If you carry your phone in your purse, backpack or pocket with change, keys or other items, the screen can easily get scratches from rubbing against those hard surfaces. This can weaken the integrity of the original display and cause cracks more easily, says Zilberman. Screen protectors are a good way to minimize cracks, scratches and shattering of your physical screen, according to the experts I spoke with. While they vary in price, most aren’t terribly expensive: Plastic ones typically cost less than $15, while glass screen protectors range from around $10 to upwards of $50. There are limitations to what a screen protector can do, though: “It isn’t going to cover every square millimeter of the glass display,” says Frederick. The protector also usually won’t protect the back, edges and corners of your phone — the experts I spoke to suggest pairing a screen protector with a heavy-duty case from brands like Casetify or Otterbox, preferably one with rubber edges that’ll absorb the impact of a drop and prevent damage. How I picked the best screen protectors Combining expert advice with my experience covering tech, I kept the following in mind when choosing the picks above: Material: Though screen protectors can be made from a variety of materials, I focused mostly on options made from tempered glass, which experts shared has excellent scratch and fall resistance.Size availability: A screen protector is only useful if it fits over the entirety of your phone screen. Every screen protector recommended is available in various sizes specific to individual phone models.Price: Screen protectors can cost an array of prices. To keep all budgets in mind, I selected products across a range of prices, from less than $10 to $60. How to shop for a screen protector When shopping for a screen protector, focus on material, comfort and ease of installation. Here’s a bit more info to keep in mind: Material: Screen protectors come in a variety of materials. There are plastics like polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), as well as tempered glass (with some even made from chemically strengthened, shatterproof glass). The experts I spoke with agree that a quality tempered glass protector will be more effective at protecting your display than plastic ones. This is because tempered glass is a stronger material that can absorb the impact if your phone falls — NBC Selected reporter Mili Godio has had her tempered glass case for more than a year and dropped her phone countless times without a scratch. Comfort and feel: We touch our phone screens to use them, so the feel and responsiveness of a screen protector is important. Screen protectors can sometimes change a phone’s touchscreen sensitivity — certain smartphone models ask you to input whether or not you’re using a screen protector on the device to better calibrate sensitivity, says Zilberman. Tempered glass is designed to have a smoother feel than other screen protectors and won’t affect touchscreen sensitivity much, according to experts. Display: Tempered glass mimics the original display of your device and offers good clarity, whereas plastic screen protectors can create an unsightly glare and affect screen quality by adding a “murkier and grayer hue to your screen,” says Zilberman. Both plastic and tempered glass protectors can have privacy and anti-glare filters to fit your preferences. However, tempered glass protectors are more physically noticeable on your screen since they’re thicker — a plastic protector blends in remarkably well with the original display, according to our experts. Ease of installation: Installing a screen protector can be difficult, especially when there’s a chance of misaligning the protector or having annoying air bubbles and specks of dust lodged underneath the film. Many screen protectors include a plastic installation tray that can go directly over your phone screen to align the protector or one that holds your phone while you guide the screen shield on. Alternatively, some protectors come with “guide stickers” showing where the screen protector will lie on your screen. Compatibility: According to Frederick, there isn’t much variation in how well a screen protector works from one smartphone brand to another. However, screen protectors come in different shapes and sizes depending on your phone, so it’s always good to check compatibility before purchasing. articles.title: Fall fashion is all about nostalgia — everyone will be rocking these '90s and '00s trends this year
articles.summary: From gaucho pants to asymmetric hemlines, here are 6 favorites from your Y2K closet that are making a comeback.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

We hope you didn't clean out your closet too thoroughly over the years, because fall is pushing some familiar fashion favorites into the spotlight. Style mavens are raiding the archives and bringing back decades-old trends we loved, forgot about and, in some cases, swore we'd never wear again. Think early-2000s gaucho pants, '90s plaid and plenty of other styles that might have you wondering what year it is. But this time around, they've gotten some updates that make them feel surprisingly current.

To find out which blasts from the past are officially ready for another moment, we tapped a team of fashion experts to reveal the six '90s and 2000s trends you'll be seeing everywhere this fall. You may even have a few of them collecting dust in the back of your closet, so consider this your sign to start digging. And if your old favorites disappeared during a long-overdue closet purge, never fear: We've rounded up plenty of fresh finds worth adding to your cart if you're ready to embrace a little fashion déjà vu.

The comfy pants you probably never expected to see again are officially back. "Gaucho pants are probably the return I am most excited about," says stylist Zoë Hennessey . "They have the ease of leggings, but I personally do not love wearing tight pants, so gaucho pants feel much more comfortable and easy for me. I didn't realize how much I missed them until they came back."

The trick to making gauchos feel more 2026 than an early-aughts throwback is all in the styling. "The wide and flowy bottoms offer movement to the overall outfit, making it a great pair with shaped pieces like a structured jacket and/or a pointed boot," says celebrity stylist Derek Warburton .

Made By Johnny High-Waist Wide-Leg Gaucho Pants

Plaid may be a perennial fall favorite, but this season, the classic pattern is getting a more grown-up makeover. Preppy pleated skirts and grungy flannel shirts are taking a back seat to fashion-forward pieces that make the traditional print feel cool again. "I expect a big comeback for all things plaid," says Warburton. "However, I think a more fashionable comeback for plaid won't come in older genres like school or grunge; instead, plaid will be reserved for more tailored and sophisticated pieces, like in trousers or blazers, and usually paired with denim pieces or knitted tops."

We recommend starting with one piece that you mix and match with modern basics. Try a plaid midi skirt with a chunky knit and boots, or pair a lightweight checkered top in an unexpected color with jeans. And for even more fresh ways to wear plaid this fall, check out this handy guide .

Prettygarden Plaid High Waisted A-Line Midi Skirt

Pilcro Hadley Relaxed Plaid Buttondown Shirt

Asymmetric hemlines are bringing back the playful, anything-goes energy of the early aughts with slinky, uneven silhouettes that instantly make an outfit more interesting. They look cool enough to wear solo now, but they're also perfect for layering with sweaters, jackets and boots once the temperatures dip.

"The nostalgia of '00s red carpet looks makes me yearn for this pre-Instagram era. Style was less about looking flawless or executing a perfectly crafted PR moment, and more about authenticity, which is what makes things cool," says Erika Kuhn, stylist at Modern Vanilla . "I love the asymmetrical hemlines from these days, which were often slinky tops or dresses layered over pants — perfect for the cooler season. It's a bonus that this hemline is extra flattering and elongates your silhouette."

Djt Flowy Handkerchief Hemline Midi Skirt

By Anthropologie Celia Asymmetric Ribbed Sweater

The peplum top — the flouncy, waist-defining silhouette that dominated the late '00s and early '10s — is officially making its way back into the fashion spotlight. Today's peplums are more sophisticated, trading sweet frills for sharper lines, sculpted shapes and a much sleeker finish. "The modern peplum creates more movement and dimension in an outfit. It also can make someone feel more feminine or whimsical, which is exactly what a lot of my clients are searching for in their personal style," says stylist Samantha Dawn .

"I never thought I'd say this, but the peplum is back!" agrees personal stylist Kelly Ostro . "After seasons of oversized, relaxed silhouettes, I think women are ready to see their waists again. I love a sculpted waist paired with something relaxed or masculine on the bottom. It's a perfect example of how fashion works: Everything eventually comes back, but it's how you style it the second time around that makes it feel new."

Brown is having a major moment this fall. "In place of the cooler neutrals that have dominated the past few autumns, richer and warmer browns are now in fashion," says Dawn Porto, chief product officer at Clarks . "Brown is the perfect color for autumn, offering warmth, depth and a sense of grounded style, which is much more interesting than yet another surge of black or gray."

But this season, brown isn't sticking to the usual autumnal playbook. Instead of going head-to-toe in chocolate or caramel, it's all about pairing the warm neutral with fresh jolts of color . Hennessey recommends wearing brown with some of the season's less expected shades, including light pink, baby blue and deep wine red. "They feel very reminiscent of the '90s to me," she says. The surprising combos make classic brown feel fresher, and prove the versatile neutral plays well with more than your typical fall palette.

Old Navy Oversized Half-Zip Performance Fleece Pullover

Remember when wearing two tank tops at once was practically a wardrobe requirement? Well, the layered-cami look is officially back. "I really love the layered tank look. Two tanks layered over each other are probably the easiest way to wear it," says Hennessey. "But as we move into cooler weather, you can layer the tanks over tees or long-sleeve tees and top everything with a blazer. I think this is also a cool way to play with color. Layering different shades over each other, maybe even adding in a sheer piece, can look very chic."

Aelfric Eden Contrast Layered Padded Cami Top

FP Movement All Clear Coastline Layered Look Tank Top

Even better, you don't necessarily have to dig through your closet and start stacking tanks to recreate the look. Brands are now doing the layering for you with clever two-in-one styles that give you that doubled-up, Y2K-inspired effect without the extra fabric or bulk, making them ideal for layering under cardigans and light jackets this fall.

articles.title: What the developer behind the Yosemite land swap wants to build
articles.summary: In his first interview on the topic, Jeff Pori said he aims to connect a new resort to a national park road by exchanging an acre of federal land for another...
articles.body:
A potential deal to enable a land swap in Yosemite National Park would allow for a driveway that would connect a lodge and rental cabins to the iconic park, the project's developer said in an interview with The Washington Post.

Jeff Pori, chief executive of Nevada-based Kingsbarn Realty Capital, shared new details about the company's goals Monday in his first press interview on the topic.

Under the proposal, Pori said, the federal government would exchange land that is part of Yosemite for property purchased by Kingsbarn so the company can connect its development to a highway lying inside the park, 700 feet away.

On its 83-acre property, the company aims to build short-term rental accommodations for tourists coming to the country's fifth-most-visited national park. Pori said it would not be a private "compound for rich guys" to live in, as some are trying to characterize it.

A lawyer representing Kingsbarn initially described plans for upscale residences, before clarifying that the plans were for rentals and not individually owned houses.

Pori said the project has yet to be designed, but the company's proposal will be similar to one made by a previous private owner from whom Kingsbarn bought the property. That plan included more than 80 cabins and a 150-room hotel, as well as parking and other amenities, according to the previous design plans.

Land advocates criticized the plan as granting access to the public park for private gain.

"It's for a massive commercial development," said Neal Desai, senior director for the Pacific region for the National Parks Conservation Association, which is opposed to the swap. "This is to help a real estate developer make a massive windfall off of property that never had direct private access to a national park, full stop ."

Kingsbarn's property sits on Yosemite's western border, with the Stanislaus National Forest along its other three sides.

Currently, the property can be accessed only by an 11-mile dirt road through the national forest, and Pori said that could be a safety issue in winter conditions.

Kingsbarn is instead seeking to build a driveway to connect the property to the park highway, Pori said. It would cross land currently owned by the Interior Department, which would give Kingsbarn 1.1 acres in exchange for property of equal value, if the deal moves forward.

Even once connected to the highway, the development would be a 45-minute-plus drive to Yosemite's valley floor or any of the other major attractions of the park, he said. The development would be hidden by a berm and not visible from the highway.

Pori said the potential new lodging area would pull some visitors away from the congested valley floor inside the park where other accommodations are located.

"It's about safety, convenience and adding something to the park so that it would be a nice place for people to come to. And the fact that it's a long way away from where the other lodging is, which is congested," Pori said.

Desai of the National Parks Conservation Association said the Kingsbarn project would do the opposite and add congestion to the already overloaded park.

"They are bringing more people to the park. They are bringing more cars to the park," Desai said.

He said congestion became far worse after the Trump administration eliminated a daily reservation system at the park that previously controlled the flow of visitors.

"We have people already waiting for hours just to get inside the park, and then they get inside the park and they spend another hour circling around looking for for parking. Yosemite right now is in complete chaos. "

Desai said he visited early on a Thursday in June, when there was a 30-minute wait at the park's entrance and already hundreds of cars competing for too few parking spots near the trailheads in the valley.

In the company's efforts to gain access to the main park highway, Pori said, he had one in-person meeting last year at the Interior Department, which referred him to National Park Service staff.

A series of Zoom calls followed, in which park staff established that a land swap would be the best way to move forward.

Kingsbarn is now in the process of having the land appraised to ensure that the swap is of equal value, Pori said. Only after the park land is appraised would Kingsbarn and the Park Service be able to identify a suitable parcel to exchange for it, Pori said.

He said the Park Service indicated that the parcel would need to be in California.

Last week, the Interior Department, which oversees the Park Service, said no final decision had been made on the matter. In a statement Tuesday, Elizabeth Peace, an Interior Department spokesperson, said that "if a more concrete proposal is submitted for consideration," it will be subject to federal law and the established review process, including opening it for public comments and completing an environmental review.

The Park Service generally transfers land only with congressional approval, with possible limited exceptions for minor adjustments to park boundaries, so long as the ultimate goal is conservation.

"A land exchange does not necessarily require a congressional appropriation if the proponent agrees to cover all associated costs," Peace said. "Depending on the appraised values of the properties involved, congressional notification or approval may be required before an exchange could be completed."

Congress established the Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) in 1964 for acquiring land and water for conservation purposes, and it currently has permanent annual funding of $900 million a year.

The administration earlier this year included the Yosemite land swap on a list sent to congressional appropriators for potential inclusion in the 2026 fiscal year's LWCF transactions, documents show. Congress has not advanced the project.

Sens. Jeff Merkley (D-Oregon) and Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska), the top-ranking lawmakers on the Senate Appropriations subcommittee for interior, provided the department with a list of projects they agreed to advance, according to Merkley spokesperson Maggie Sunstrum.

"That didn't include the Yosemite project, which Senator Merkley objected to," she said.

Murkowski's office did not respond to request for comment.

The office of Sen. Alex Padilla (D-California) is aware of the administration's attempt to transfer part of Yosemite to a private developer, spokesperson Danny Rodriguez said in a statement.

"Our office is working with staff on the Senate Appropriations Committee to try to block the Interior Department from moving this project forward," Rodriguez said.

The Park Service property in question is in Tuolumne and Mariposa counties, but the land acquired in exchange "may be in a different county," the submission to Congress said, without elaborating on the possible location.

Desai said that if the land exchange is allowed for reasons that are commercial rather than conservation-related, it would set a dangerous precedent.

articles.title: Teatro Amazonas recebe alunos do projeto Pipoca em Cena em Manaus | G1
articles.standfirst: Visita guiada promovida pela Fundação Rede Amazônica integrou a programação da 12ª edição do projeto e aproximou os alunos da cultura, da arquitetura e da história de Manaus.
articles.summary: A visita guiada da Fundação Rede Amazônica aproximou alunos da cultura e arquitetura de Manaus durante a 12ª edição do projeto Pipoca em Cena no Teatro Amazonas.
articles.body:
'Um lugar muito lindo': estudantes do Pipoca em Cena mergulham na história do Teatro Amazonas — Foto: Foto: João Paulo Oliveira/FRAM

Conhecer um dos cartões-postais de Manaus pode ser algo comum para muita gente, mas, para quem ainda está descobrindo a própria cidade, a experiência pode ganhar outro significado. Foi assim para os estudantes do Pipoca em Cena que, nesta quarta-feira (2), deixaram a sala de aula para conhecer de perto o Teatro Amazonas. Duas turmas da Escola Estadual Cívico-Militar Fueth Paulo Mourão, no bairro São Jorge, zona Oeste de Manaus, participaram de visitas guiadas realizadas pela manhã e à tarde.

Durante o tour, os alunos passaram por diferentes espaços do teatro e acompanharam explicações sobre a construção do prédio, a arquitetura e acontecimentos que fazem parte da história do local e da capital amazonense. Para alguns, era a primeira vez dentro do Teatro Amazonas — e as descobertas começaram logo na chegada.

“Estou sendo impactado com essa vista porque é um lugar muito lindo. Aqui a gente aprende mais sobre a história de Manaus. A guia mostrou como foi criado o teatro e falou um pouco mais da nossa história”, contou Natanael Cassotti, de 14 anos.

A arquitetura foi um dos detalhes que mais chamou a atenção. Geovanna Dias, de 15 anos, também estava pela primeira vez no interior do teatro e aproveitou a visita para observar de perto elementos que tornam o espaço tão conhecido.

“Eu estou gostando muito da visita e aprendendo muita coisa sobre o teatro e a arquitetura. O que eu mais estou gostando é a arquitetura, que é muito bonita e chama muita atenção”, disse.

Se nas oficinas do Pipoca em Cena os estudantes aprendem a criar e contar histórias por meio do audiovisual, no Teatro Amazonas eles encontraram um lugar que também carrega muitas delas. A cada espaço visitado, a arquitetura e as explicações da guia ajudaram a transformar o passeio em uma aula sobre a cidade.

A visita é uma novidade na programação da 12ª edição do projeto. A proposta da Fundação Rede Amazônica é ampliar as experiências oferecidas aos participantes e aproximá-los de espaços que fazem parte da história, da cultura e da identidade de Manaus.

“É uma área de grande importância para a nossa capital, principalmente na parte turística. Muitas pessoas passam pelo Centro, mas nunca tiveram a oportunidade de conhecer o teatro por dentro. Então, estamos dando essa oportunidade para esses estudantes conhecerem o Teatro Amazonas e fomentando a nossa cultura”, explicou Adriano Aguiar, especialista de projetos da Fundação Rede Amazônica.

A experiência também se conecta com a proposta de formação do Pipoca em Cena. O projeto utiliza o audiovisual como ferramenta de aprendizado, criatividade, expressão artística e protagonismo juvenil. Ao longo das atividades, os estudantes criam roteiros, participam das gravações e conhecem diferentes etapas da produção de um filme.

A experiência no Teatro Amazonas continua nesta quinta-feira (3). Desta vez, duas turmas da Escola Estadual Francelina Assis Dantas, no bairro Alvorada 2, participam das visitas guiadas, também nos períodos da manhã e da tarde.

A atividade segue a mesma proposta de aproximar os estudantes de espaços culturais de Manaus e proporcionar uma experiência de aprendizado fora da sala de aula.

Depois das oficinas, das gravações e das experiências culturais, chega a hora de conferir o resultado de todo esse processo. Os 20 curtas-metragens produzidos pelos estudantes serão exibidos nos dias 9 e 10 de setembro, durante a programação de encerramento da 12ª edição do Pipoca em Cena.

Além dos filmes produzidos pelos próprios alunos, a programação terá entrega de certificados, distribuição de pipoca e refrigerante e exibição de um filme da Globo Filmes, parceira do projeto.

O Pipoca em Cena é uma iniciativa da Fundação Rede Amazônica que utiliza o audiovisual como ferramenta de formação, expressão artística e protagonismo juvenil. Nesta 12ª edição, cerca de cem estudantes de duas escolas públicas de Manaus participam das atividades e produzem 20 curtas-metragens com histórias relacionadas ao meio ambiente e à sustentabilidade.

A programação reúne oficinas de produção audiovisual, experiências culturais, exibição dos filmes produzidos pelos alunos e atividades de encerramento. O projeto conta com apoio da Eucatur Urbano e da Globo Filmes.

articles.summary: Com entrada gratuita, o evento começa nesta sexta(4) e segue até segunda-feira (7) com shows, rodeio e atrações para a família.
articles.body:
Expo Paraíba do Sul tem shows de Samuel Eleoterio, Xamã, Cabelinho, Marcos & Belutti e Panda. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A 46ª Expo Paraíba do Sul começa nesta sexta-feira (4) com entrada gratuita no Parque de Exposições Antônio Avelino de Oliveira, em Paraíba do Sul (RJ), e segue com a programação até segunda-feira (7). O evento reúne grandes nomes da música nacional, rodeio da Cia. Falcão e o tradicional concurso leiteiro.

Segundo a organização, na abertura, na sexta-feira (4), o público acompanha o show gospel do cantor Samuel Eleotério. No sábado (5), sobem ao palco os rappers Xamã e MC Cabelinho. No domingo (6), a atração principal é a dupla sertaneja Marcos & Belutti. O encerramento, na segunda-feira (7), fica por conta do cantor Panda.

De sábado a segunda-feira, a arena recebe o rodeio da Cia. Falcão. Além das apresentações musicais, o evento conta com parque de diversões, fazendinha, tradicional Concurso Leiteiro, atrações infantis, Centro de Convenções e feira de artesanato.

Esta é a segunda edição da Expo Paraíba do Sul desde a retomada do evento, em 2025, após um intervalo de quase dez anos sem a realização da festa.

articles.title: Menino de bicicleta elétrica fica ferido após ser atingido por moto em Rorainópolis | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima, de 10 anos, fraturou a clavícula e foi levada ao hospital da região. Acidente foi em cruzamento.
articles.summary: Vítima, de 10 anos, fraturou a clavícula e foi levada ao hospital da região. Acidente foi em cruzamento.
articles.body:
Um menino de 10 anos ficou ferido após ser atingido por uma motocicleta enquanto pilotava uma bicicleta elétrica , na tarde desta terça-feira (1º), na avenida Ayrton Senna, em Rorainópolis, no Sul de Roraima.

A Rede Amazônica apurou que o menino fraturou a clavícula. Ele foi socorrido pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e levado ao hospital de Rorainópolis, onde recebeu atendimento e foi liberado ainda no mesmo dia.

O acidente ocorreu em um cruzamento, próximo a um restaurante e um supermercado. Testemunha relataram que a batida ocorreu porque o menino entrou na avenida e o motociclista não conseguiu desviar a tempo.

Uma pessoa que estava no estabelecimento foi até a rua para ajudar o menino e acionou o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu). O motociclista teve apenas ferimentos leves.

articles.title: Trump diz que Venezuela não está pronta para novas eleições | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente dos EUA também elogiou trabalho de Delcy Rodríguez. Governo e oposição venezuelanos discutem transição pacífica de poder.
articles.summary: Presidente dos EUA também elogiou trabalho de Delcy Rodríguez. Governo e oposição venezuelanos discutem transição pacífica de poder.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , afirmou nesta quarta-feira (2) que a Venezuela ainda não está pronta para realizar eleições. Ele também elogiou o governo da presidente interina Delcy Rodríguez.

A Venezuela está sob um governo interino desde a captura do ex-ditador Nicolás Maduro. Ele foi preso durante uma operação dos EUA no país, em 3 de janeiro.

Após a queda de Maduro, Delcy, que era vice-presidente, assumiu o controle do país. Desde então, ela tem atendido a pedidos dos Estados Unidos e ampliado o diálogo com Trump.

Enquanto isso, governo e oposição negociam uma transição pacífica de poder, com mediação dos Estados Unidos. Para Trump, no entanto, o país ainda não está pronto para realizar uma nova eleição.

"Simplesmente não me parece que eles estejam prontos ainda. Sabe, é algo muito recente. Nós os tiramos de uma ditadura e estamos nos dando muito bem com o governo", disse.

Logo depois, em uma declaração na Venezuela, Delcy disse que o país só terá eleições quando estiver "pronto".

A presidente interina também agradeceu Trump pelo um acordo energético fechado entre os dois países na semana passada. Segundo Delcy, a medida trará "bem-estar" para a Venezuela.

O acordo concede aos EUA o controle de 65 bilhões de barris das reservas de petróleo da Venezuela em 17 campos do país. Segundo Delcy, os negócios renderão US$ 209 bilhões (R$ 1,1 trilhão) em 25 anos.

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, e a presidente interina da Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez — Foto: REUTERS/Kevin Lamarque / Wendys Olivo/Palácio Miraflores/Divulgação via REUTERS

articles.title: Trump cita 'boa relação com o Brasil' e afirma ter feito 'muita gente ser eleita' na América do Sul: 'Estão todos indo para a direita'  | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente dos EUA não mencionou presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e disse que relação dos EUA com América do Sul vem melhorando porque 'estão todos indo para a direita'.
articles.summary: Presidente dos EUA não mencionou presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e disse que relação dos EUA com América do Sul vem melhorando porque 'estão todos indo para a direita'.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, em entrevista no Salão Oval da Casa Branca, em 2 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Evelyn Hockstein/ Reuters

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, disse nesta quarta-feira (3) que tem uma "boa relação com o Brasil" atualmente . Ele não citou, no entanto, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), e disse ter ajudado "muita gente a ser eleita na América do Sul" recentemente.

Em entrevista a jornalistas na Casa Branca, Trump afirmou ainda que as relações dos EUA com toda a América do Sul têm melhorado e citou, como motivo, que "estão todos indo para a direita".

"Eles deixaram a esquerda e foram para a direita; estão todos indo para a direita. Temos um bom relacionamento com o Brasil. Na verdade, temos um bom relacionamento com praticamente todos eles agora. Eles têm muito respeito pelo nosso país. Eles não respeitavam nosso país nem um pouco há dois anos, então estamos indo muito bem na América do Sul, na América Latina", afirmou.

Questionado se pretende construir bases militares na América do Sul por conta das recentes parcerias com governos de países como Colômbia e El Salvador, Trump não respondeu especificamente. Mas citou a influência que afirma que vem tendo em eleições no continente.

"Temos muitas pessoas — na Argentina, por exemplo, há muitas pessoas que ajudei a eleger — e essa parte do nosso hemisfério está realmente se tornando muito diferente do que era", afirmou o norte-americano.

articles.title: 7 de Setembro no Rio: O que abre e fecha e horários do transporte | G1
articles.standfirst: Metrô, VLT, barcas e rodovias terão operação especial; agências do INSS não funcionam na segunda-feira (7)
articles.summary: Metrô, VLT e barcas operam com horários especiais no feriado de 7 de Setembro no Rio, que terá agências do INSS fechadas e unidades de saúde 24h abertas.
articles.body:
Desfile de 7 de setembro no Rio de Janeiro acontece na Avenida Presidente Vargas — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

O feriado de 7 de Setembro, na próxima segunda-feira (7), vai alterar o funcionamento de serviços e do transporte público no Rio. Metrô, VLT e barcas terão esquemas especiais por causa do desfile cívico-militar no Centro e dos shows do Rock in Rio 2026. As agências do INSS estarão fechadas, e as principais rodovias devem registrar aumento no movimento.

Confira abaixo o que funciona e o que muda no feriado:

O MetrôRio vai funcionar das 7h às 23h, como ocorre normalmente em feriados. As linhas 1 e 4 circularão entre Uruguai e Jardim Oceânico, enquanto a Linha 2 fará o trajeto entre Pavuna e Botafogo. Para o Rock in Rio, os acessos B (Mar) e C (BRT) da estação Jardim Oceânico ficarão abertos 24 horas para embarque. As demais estações permanecerão abertas durante a madrugada apenas para desembarque do público do festival, entre 23h de segunda e 5h de terça-feira (8). A tarifa custa R$ 7,90 por trecho.

As barcas vão operar com a grade de domingos e feriados. A linha Praça XV–Arariboia terá funcionamento das 6h às 23h, com partidas a cada hora, e no sentido Arariboia–Praça XV, das 5h30 às 23h30. As linhas Charitas e Cocotá não funcionarão. A ligação com Paquetá terá horários específicos ao longo do dia.

O VLT Carioca terá operação especial por causa do desfile e dos bloqueios de vias no Centro. As Linhas 1 e 4 funcionarão parcialmente, entre Terminal Gentileza e Parada dos Museus e entre Terminal Gentileza e Central, respectivamente. A Linha 3 circulará entre Santos Dumont e Cinelândia, com intervalos médios de 20 minutos. Já a Linha 2, entre Praia Formosa e Praça XV, ficará suspensa temporariamente. A operação completa será retomada após o fim do desfile e a liberação das vias.

Todas as agências do INSS estarão fechadas na segunda-feira (7). O atendimento presencial será retomado na terça-feira (8). Durante o feriado, a Central 135 terá apenas atendimento eletrônico . O site e o aplicativo Meu INSS continuarão disponíveis 24 horas.

A Secretaria Municipal de Saúde (SMS) informa que as unidades 24 horas da rede municipal de saúde – UPAs, hospitais, centros de emergência regional (CERs) e centros de atenção psicossocial (CAPS) tipo III – vão funcionar ininterruptamente durante o feriado da Independência do Brasil, dia 7 setembro.

O Super Centro Carioca de Vacinação de Botafogo funcionará normalmente no feriado. As unidades do Super Centro Carioca de Vacinação da Zona Oeste, no ParkShoppingCampoGrande, e da Zona Norte, no Shopping Nova América, funcionarão de acordo com os horários dos centros comerciais.

As demais unidades, como centros municipais de saúde, clínicas da família e policlínicas não irão funcionar no dia do feriado, retomando as atividades normalmente na terça-feira, dia 8 de setembro

articles.title: Quem faz a curadoria das suas compras? A escolha certa vale mais do que muitas opções | G1
articles.standfirst: Cresce a procura por orientação especializada na hora de comprar diante de tantas opções de vinhos, cafés especiais, queijos artesanais e produtos gourmet.
articles.summary: Cresce a procura por orientação especializada na hora de comprar diante de tantas opções de vinhos, cafés especiais, queijos artesanais e produtos gourmet.
articles.body:
Diante da prateleira de vinhos, a dúvida aparece rápido. Um rótulo premiado, outro produzido por uma vinícola centenária, um terceiro recomendado por um amigo. A cena se repete no corredor dos cafés, dos azeites, dos queijos artesanais ou das massas. Nunca foi tão fácil encontrar produtos de qualidade. Também nunca foi tão difícil decidir qual levar para casa.

O aumento da oferta mudou a forma como muita gente faz compras. Em vez de procurar apenas variedade, consumidores pesquisam e passam a valorizar alguém que conheça profundamente o que está sendo vendido. A confiança na recomendação ganhou espaço ao lado da qualidade dos produtos.

Essa lógica explica por que supermercados premium passaram a investir em profissionais capazes de orientar escolhas, sugerir harmonizações e apresentar ingredientes que, muitas vezes, passariam despercebidos entre tantas opções.

Para quem gosta de cozinhar ou receber amigos, a diferença entre uma compra comum e uma experiência memorável costuma estar nos detalhes.

Um vinho pode mudar completamente de acordo com a uva, a região onde foi produzido ou o prato que ele vai acompanhar. O mesmo acontece com cafés especiais, queijos maturados, massas artesanais e embutidos. A curadoria faz sentido justamente neste momento.

Ela reduz o tempo gasto comparando produtos, ajuda a descobrir novas marcas e oferece segurança para quem deseja experimentar ingredientes diferentes sem depender apenas da embalagem ou do preço.

Por trás de uma boa compra existe uma seleção cuidadosa de marcas, produtores e especialistas. Conheça como a curadoria foi pensada para reunir gastronomia, qualidade e atendimento em um só lugar. Confira o que o Ítalo Barigui pode oferecer.

Empórios inspiram a tendência da curadoria

Durante muito tempo, esse tipo de atendimento era encontrado principalmente em empórios especializados, adegas ou lojas dedicadas a um único segmento.

Ali, era comum conversar com alguém que conhecia os produtores, explicava as diferenças entre os produtos e sugeria combinações para cada ocasião.

Nos últimos anos, esse modelo começou a aparecer também em supermercados voltados à gastronomia e à curadoria de alimentos, aproximando conhecimento técnico da rotina de quem faz as compras da semana.

A escolha de um bom vinho pode ser bem mais tranquila com a presença de um expert. — Foto: Divulgação/Ítalo Barigui.

Esse conceito orienta a proposta do Supermercado Conceito Ítalo Barigui , inaugurado na região do Barigui.

Um dos diferenciais é o Concierge Ítalo , serviço gratuito em que um consultor acompanha o cliente durante as compras, auxiliando na escolha de produtos de acordo com cada necessidade, ocasião ou preferência.

Na adega, especialistas ajudam na seleção de vinhos e harmonizações, aproximando um atendimento normalmente associado a casas especializadas da rotina do supermercado.

A curadoria também aparece na escolha dos parceiros que fazem parte do empreendimento. A culinária japonesa do Taisho , os cafés especiais da Distinto , Lucca e Moka Club , a confeitaria da Délices de Sucre , as massas artesanais da L'Artigiana e Rosmarino , os temperos da Cipria , os pescados da Trapiche , a seleção de produtos importados e a floricultura compõem um ambiente onde cada marca foi escolhida por sua especialidade.

Escolher um bom produto começa muito antes de colocá-lo no carrinho. Descubra algumas das marcas e dos parceiros que ajudam a construir a experiência gastronômica do Supermercado Conceito Ítalo Barigui.

Escolher bem também faz parte da experiência

Uma boa compra nem sempre termina com o carrinho cheio. Muitas vezes, ela termina com a certeza de que aquele vinho combina com o jantar planejado, que o queijo escolhido valoriza a tábua preparada para os convidados ou que uma massa artesanal dispensa receitas complicadas para resultar em uma boa refeição.

Quando isso acontece, a curadoria deixa de ser um serviço complementar e passa a integrar a própria experiência de consumo.

É essa filosofia que orienta os cinco pilares do Supermercado Conceito Ítalo Barigui: qualidade, curadoria, praticidade, saudabilidade e proximidade.

articles.title: Fernando de Noronha reforça segurança com guarda-vidas e ambulância | G1
articles.standfirst: Sete profissionais passam a atuar nas praias do Meio e do Boldró. Já o Parque Nacional Marinho ganhou veículo para atendimentos de emergência.
articles.summary: Sete profissionais passam a atuar nas praias do Meio e do Boldró. Já o  Parque Nacional Marinho ganhou veículo para atendimentos de emergência.
articles.body:
Fernando de Noronha reforçou a segurança nas praias da Área de Proteção Ambiental (APA). Sete guarda-vidas foram contratados para atuar nas praias do Meio e do Boldró. Já o Parque Nacional Marinho recebeu uma ambulância para atendimentos de emergência nesta terça-feira (1º).

As medidas têm como objetivo ampliar a prevenção e o socorro em casos de acidentes na ilha ( veja vídeo acima ).

Novos salva-vidas trabalham nas praias do Meio e Boldró — Foto: Ana Clara Marinho/TV Globo

Os novos guarda-vidas civis foram contratados pela Administração da Ilha. A equipe trabalha todos os dias, das 9h às 17h. Segundo o governo local, os profissionais atuam na prevenção de acidentes, orientação aos visitantes, fiscalização e salvamento.

A equipe também acompanha o acesso ao Buraco do Galego, na Praia do Cachorro. Os guarda-vidas orientam os visitantes sobre as condições do mar e os riscos durante o acesso ao local.

O Corpo de Bombeiros Militar de Pernambuco (CBMPE) mantém três postos fixos de guarda-vidas, nas praias do Porto de Santo Antônio, do Cachorro e da Conceição, que também fazem parte da APA.

Os guarda-vidas trabalham nas praias da APA da ilha — Foto: Weidson Carlos/Administração de Fernando de Noronha

Em março deste ano, os turistas Lucas Henrique Abrunhosa Nozoe, de 31 anos , e Glenda Moraes da Silva, de 29, morreram após se afogarem na Praia do Meio.

Os dois eram médicos. Lucas morreu no dia do afogamento, em 9 de março. Glenda foi transferida para o Recife, mas não resistiu e morreu no dia 16 de março.

O Parque Nacional Marinho passou a contar com uma ambulância e equipe para atendimento de emergência. A medida faz parte da ampliação do sistema de segurança da reserva, que passou a ser responsabilidade da concessionária EcoNoronha.

O parque é administrado pelo Instituto Chico Mendes de Conservação da Biodiversidade ( ICMBio ). O contrato da concessionária foi prorrogado pelo órgão federal por mais cinco anos em novembro de 2025. A partir daí, começaram a ser implantadas novas medidas de segurança:

Entre as medidas foram realizadas as seguintes ações:

aplicação de protocolos de operação, iniciada em 1º de julho;

implantação de um sistema de atendimento a emergências;

contratação de equipe de enfermagem e de motoristas socorristas, a partir de 17 de agosto;

aquisição de uma ambulância para reforçar o atendimento de emergência.

Segundo a concessionária, ainda neste mês de setembro será implantado de um sistema de atendimento a emergências aquáticas.

articles.title: Embraer E-Jets: marca histórica de 2.000 aviões é atingida | G1
articles.standfirst: Aeronaves são produzidas em São José dos Campos e já acumularam 48 milhões de horas de voo em todo o mundo.
articles.summary: Embraer E-Jets atingem a marca histórica de 2.000 entregas mundiais com aeronave recebida pela Azul, somando 48 milhões de horas de voo desde 2004.
articles.body:
A Embraer alcançou nesta quarta-feira (2) a marca de 2.000 aviões entregues da família E-Jets. O modelo de número 2.000 saiu da fábrica de São José dos Campos , no interior de SP, e foi entregue à Azul.

Desde a primeira entrega, em 2004, os E-Jets já acumularam 48 milhões de horas de voo e transportaram mais de 2,85 bilhões de passageiros.

A marca coloca a família entre os três programas de aviões comerciais com mais entregas no mundo.

Os jatos foram desenvolvidos principalmente para rotas regionais, em que aeronaves maiores nem sempre são viáveis. Hoje, mais de 90 companhias aéreas já operaram os modelos em mais de 60 países.

A Azul recebeu a aeronave comemorativa. A companhia já operou 145 aviões da Embraer e tem outras 25 encomendas previstas até 2029.

O presidente da Azul, John Rodgerson, afirmou que a empresa está animada com as próximas entregas e que os aviões podem abrir espaço para novas rotas.

Entre os exemplos citados está a possibilidade de uma ligação entre Recife e Porto Alegre.

“Estamos sempre olhando novas rotas, conectividade, alcance dessa aeronave. Por exemplo, podemos fazer Recife-Porto Alegre facilmente".

2.000º jato da família E-Jets da Embraer é entregue em São José dos Campos, no interior de São Paulo. — Foto: Bruna Capasciutti/Rede Vanguarda

O papel dos E-Jets na aviação regional foi destacado pelo ministro de Portos e Aeroportos, Tomé Franca.

Segundo ele, o tamanho dos aviões permite atender à demanda de cidades que não necessariamente comportam aeronaves maiores.

“Esse é um avião que consegue trazer capilaridade, maior conectividade para as cidades brasileiras.”

O ministro também afirmou que o governo tem ampliado os investimentos em aeroportos regionais. Segundo ele, mais de R$ 10 bilhões foram investidos em aeroportos brasileiros nos últimos três anos e meio.

Entre abril e junho, a Embraer entregou 65 aeronaves, o melhor resultado para um segundo trimestre em 16 anos. A carteira de pedidos também chegou a US$ 34,5 bilhões, sendo US$ 15,1 bilhões na aviação comercial, com 465 aviões ainda a serem entregues.

O CEO da Embraer, Francisco Gomes Neto, afirmou que a empresa vive uma fase de crescimento sustentável desde 2021 e espera alcançar novos recordes em 2026.

“Esse ano aqui a gente, entregando nosso gate para o mercado, vamos de novo fazer recorde de receita, de rentabilidade, de entregas. Então, um ano muito bom.”

A fabricante prevê entregar entre 240 e 250 aeronaves neste ano, somando os segmentos comercial e executivo.

Para os próximos anos, a empresa também estuda um novo ciclo de produtos e tecnologias. Segundo Gomes Neto, a Embraer avalia quais caminhos seguir para a próxima geração de aeronaves.

“Estamos estudando um novo ciclo de produtos da companhia, fazendo muitos estudos, estamos investindo em novas tecnologias e estudando qual vai ser o caminho do novo ciclo para a Embraer.”

Apesar da boa fase, o fornecimento de componentes ainda é um desafio. O CEO afirmou que existem pontos da cadeia de fornecedores que dificultam a produção no prazo planejado, mas disse que a empresa espera cumprir as entregas previstas para 2026.

articles.title: Morte de peixes em lagoa de Divinópolis leva à investigação sobre qualidade da água | G1
articles.standfirst: Vistoria técnica encontrou sinais de excesso de nutrientes na água. Proprietário da área particular deverá custear a análise da lagoa, segundo a Prefeitura.
articles.summary: Vistoria técnica encontrou sinais de excesso de nutrientes na água. Como a lagoa fica em uma propriedade particular, o dono do imóvel deverá custear a análise, segundo a Prefeitura
articles.body:
Fiscalização identificou peixes mortos nessa lagoa, em Divinópolis — Foto: Prefeitura de Divinópolis/Divulgação

A morte de peixes em uma lagoa no bairro Icaraí, em Divinópolis , levou a Prefeitura a iniciar uma investigação sobre as condições da água . Uma vistoria técnica realizada na terça-feira (1º) encontrou sinais de eutrofização na água.

🔎 Eutrofização é o processo de poluição de um corpo d’água causado pelo excesso de nutrientes, principalmente fósforo e nitrogênio. O acúmulo dessas substâncias provoca a multiplicação descontrolada de algas e plantas aquáticas.

A fiscalização, realizada pela Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente e Cuidado Animal (Semac), avaliou as condições ambientais da lagoa, que fica em uma propriedade particular. O nome do proprietário não foi divulgado.

Durante a vistoria, os técnicos identificaram excesso de nutrientes na água. No entanto, segundo a Prefeitura, ainda não é possível determinar o que provocou a morte dos peixes .

Como parte da fiscalização, o responsável pela propriedade será formalmente notificado para arcar com a análise completa da qualidade da água.

A medida tem como base o Decreto Municipal nº 4.748 , que permite à Semac determinar aos responsáveis por possíveis fontes de poluição a realização de medições e análises ambientais, sem custos para o Município.

Serão analisados fatores como a baixa concentração de oxigênio na água, processos naturais de estratificação, eventual inversão térmica, alterações nos parâmetros físico-químicos e um possível lançamento de substâncias ou efluentes na lagoa.

O exame deverá avaliar parâmetros físico-químicos e microbiológicos e ser realizado por laboratório ou empresa tecnicamente habilitada, com acompanhamento da fiscalização municipal.

Após receber os laudos, a Prefeitura fará a avaliação dos resultados e das condições ambientais da lagoa.

Caso sejam identificadas irregularidades, poderão ser adotadas medidas administrativas e ambientais previstas na legislação.

articles.title: Moradores denunciam falta de iluminação em ruas de Petrópolis | G1
articles.standfirst: Problema é relatado nas ruas Padre Moreira e Deputado Romão Júnior; moradores afirmam que postes apresentam falhas e luzes piscam durante a chuva.
articles.summary: Problema é relatado nas ruas Padre Moreira e Deputado Romão Júnior; moradores afirmam que postes apresentam falhas e luzes piscam durante a chuva.
articles.body:
Moradores do Centro de Petrópolis , na Região Serrana do Rio, denunciam problemas na iluminação pública em duas importantes vias da cidade: as ruas Padre Moreira e Deputado Romão Júnior. Segundo relatos, a iluminação é insuficiente e apresenta instabilidade, principalmente durante períodos de chuva.

De acordo com moradores, algumas lâmpadas dos postes deixam de funcionar ao anoitecer e, quando chove, as que permanecem acesas passam a piscar constantemente.

Na Rua Padre Moreira está localizado o Trono de Fátima, um dos pontos turísticos mais conhecidos do município. Em registros feitos por moradores, é possível observar oscilações na iluminação da área durante momentos de chuva.

Moradores afirmam que postes apresentam falhas e luzes piscam durante a chuva. — Foto: Divulgação

A situação também é relatada na Rua Deputado Romão Júnior, via de acesso à Casa de Santos Dumont, outro importante ponto turístico da cidade. Segundo os moradores, o trecho enfrenta problemas semelhantes de iluminação.

"Há meses que estamos passando por essa situação. Todo dia, depois das 17h ou 18h, fica tudo escuro. Existem poucas luzes na rua e, quando chove, elas começam a piscar. Parece uma discoteca", afirmou um morador que preferiu não se identificar.

Além da falta de iluminação, moradores relatam preocupação com a segurança na região. Segundo eles, a sensação de insegurança aumentou nos últimos meses.

As duas vias ligam o Centro ao bairro Valparaíso e também são utilizadas por motoristas como rota alternativa para evitar congestionamentos. Apesar do fluxo intenso em alguns horários, a circulação de pessoas e veículos diminui durante a noite.

"Tem que andar atento o tempo todo. Nunca sabemos quando pode aparecer alguém para assaltar ou fazer algo pior. Aqui já foi melhor para morar, está cada dia pior", disse o morador.

Segundo os relatos, reclamações já foram encaminhadas ao setor de Iluminação Pública da Prefeitura de Petrópolis. Os moradores afirmam ainda que tentaram consultar a situação dos postes por meio do portal disponibilizado pelo município, mas não encontraram os pontos de iluminação da região no sistema.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Prefeitura de Petrópolis e aguarda um posicionamento sobre as reclamações.

articles.summary: US Streamers News: TheBurntPeanut is facing backlash after a joke made during an Escape from Tarkov stream turned into a wider discussion online. The incident happened o.
articles.body: TheBurntPeanut is facing backlash after a joke made during an Escape from Tarkov stream turned into a wider discussion online. The incident happened on September 1, 2026, when the streamer was looting in the game and came across an LM-KC 130 model aircraft. What followed was a short moment on stream that viewers clipped and shared, with some users on X accusing him of making light of the deaths connected to 9/11. The backlash centered around how he staged the joke inside the game. Peanut moved the small aircraft across his screen while making airplane noises. He then arranged a magazine and a bottle in his inventory so they looked like two towers. After moving the plane toward them, he shouted, “Boom! They hit the second tower! (Laughs)” The clip became the main point of criticism around the streamer’s recent comments.Why TheBurntPeanut’s Tarkov moment caused backlashThe joke happened while Peanut was playing Escape from Tarkov, the game that has taken up more than 58% of his streaming time so far. Around 7,000 viewers watch him on average when he plays the tactical extraction shooter.That made the moment especially easy to circulate, as the clip showed exactly what happened instead of relying on a long explanation. X users then gave mixed reactions. One user, @_Kushmas, criticized the joke by saying, “this dude is the least funny personality I have ever witnessed, I don’t get why all these fu**in retards praise him.” Others were less serious about it. @JayNabbZ called it “It's actually just dark humor when someone who actually loves this country makes a joke like this.”Those reactions show the split in how the clip was received. Some viewers treated it as offensive because of what the imagery referenced, while others mainly dismissed the joke as simply bad.The HasanAbi connection goes back to February 2026There is also an older piece of context involving Hasan “HasanAbi” Piker. Months before the Tarkov incident, TheBurntPeanut had already become part of a Hasan discussion after reacting to a viewer who wrote, “USA is a joke.”Hasan responded by calling Peanut the “number one streamer of Israel” and referred to one of Peanut’s takes about “America number one” as something he found notable. His comments did not stop there.Hasan later compared Peanut to a new version of DrDisRespect, describing it as an attempt to get “DrDisRespect, but without the kid-di**ling.” That older commentary has now been brought back into discussions about Peanut after the September 1 stream.For now, the controversy remains centered on the clip from Escape from Tarkov and the criticism surrounding the joke. articles.title: Meet Carter Grandbois, the 18-year-old who started hauling junk at 16; his Colorado business now bills up to $15,000 a month
articles.summary: US News: At 16, while many of his classmates were thinking about part-time jobs in retail or food service, Carter Grandbois saw an opportunity in other people’.
articles.body: At 16, while many of his classmates were thinking about part-time jobs in retail or food service, Carter Grandbois saw an opportunity in other people’s clutter. Living in Colorado Springs, he borrowed a trailer, posted on social media and started hauling away junk for neighbours and local businesses. Two years later, at 18, he runs a growing junk-removal company that can bill as much as $15,000 in a busy month, all while finishing high school and planning his next moves. His story, as told to Fortune, shows how a simple service business, combined with savvy use of social media and a strong work ethic, can turn a teenager’s side hustle into a serious income stream.Spotting a gap in the marketCarter Grandbois grew up in a family that valued hard work and self-reliance. As a kid, he helped with yard work, moved furniture and learned basic handyman skills from relatives and neighbours. By middle school, he was already thinking about ways to make money on his own terms.The idea for a junk-removal business came from everyday observation. He noticed that people in his community often had piles of unwanted items: old furniture, appliances, construction debris, yard waste—but didn’t want to deal with the hassle of loading, hauling and dumping them. Professional junk-removal services existed, but they could be expensive or slow to respond, especially for smaller jobs.Carter realised he could fill that gap: offer fast, affordable junk hauling with a personal touch, marketed directly through the platforms where his neighbours already spent time.Starting with a borrowed trailerAt 16, Carter launched his business with minimal equipment. He did not have the capital to buy a truck or a dedicated trailer, so he borrowed a trailer from a family friend and used a vehicle he could access to tow it. His initial “marketing” was simple: posts on Facebook, Instagram and local community groups advertising junk removal, yard clean-ups and small move-out jobs. Early customers were neighbours, friends of his parents and people who saw his posts online. He priced jobs competitively, often undercutting larger companies while emphasising speed and reliability. If a customer needed something gone the same day or next day, Carter made it happen.Word spread quickly. Satisfied customers recommended him to others, and his social media feeds filled with before-and-after photos of cleared garages, cleaned-out basements and tidied-up yards.Building a brand on social mediaOne of Carter’s key advantages was his comfort with social media. As a Gen Z teenager, he understood how to use short videos, reels and photo carousels to showcase his work. He posted: time-lapse videos of junk removals, showing messy spaces transformed in minutes; before-and-after photos that clearly demonstrated the value he provided; and short clips explaining his process, pricing and service area.He also encouraged customers to tag him or share his posts when he completed a job, creating a ripple effect in local online groups. Over time, his accounts became a de facto portfolio: anyone wondering whether to hire him could scroll through months of completed projects. His online presence meant he could reach customers beyond his immediate area – serving small businesses, landlords and property managers who needed regular clean-outs. From solo operator to small team As demand grew, Carter quickly hit the limits of what one person with a borrowed trailer could do. He started buying his own equipment, like a more reliable trailer and eventually a truck just for hauling. He also began hiring people on a per-job basis, bringing in friends or acquaintances willing to work on weekends and after school. Instead of building a large, fixed payroll, he kept his team flexible, adding more people for big jobs and scaling down during slower periods. This helped him to manage costs while still being able to take on multiple jobs in a single day.By 17, Carter was no longer just the guy with a trailer; he was running a small business with a brand, a customer base and a growing reputation in the Colorado Springs area.Hitting $15,000 monthsAt 18, Carter says his business can bill up to $15,000 in a busy month, depending on the season and the number of large jobs he books. Spring and summer tend to be peak times, as people clean out garages, prepare homes for sale and tackle yard projects. Fall and winter can be slower, but there is still steady demand from landlords, contractors and businesses.Revenue comes from a mix of residential and commercial jobs: homeowners clearing out estates, moving or decluttering; landlords cleaning units between tenants; contractors removing construction debris and old materials; and small businesses disposing of old furniture, equipment and packaging.He prices jobs based on volume, weight and labour, often giving quotes from photos sent by customers. That efficiency allows him to book multiple jobs per day and keep his trucks and trailers moving.Balancing school, work and future plansRunning a business while finishing high school is not without challenges. Carter has had to manage to scheduling jobs around classes, exams and extracurricular activities; handle customer communications, estimates and invoicing in his spare time; and decide how much to reinvest in equipment versus saving for future goals, as per the report. He has talked about the pressure of being self-employed at such a young age but also the freedom it gives him to set his own hours and pick his jobs. For the future he is considering options such as expanding his service area, adding more trucks and crew members or even looking into related services such as light demolition, yard work or moving assistance. What makes his model work Carter’s success is not simply about hard work; it’s about a business model that fits his community and his strengths. For other young people looking to start a business, his story suggests you do not need a tech startup or a novel invention to build something profitable; sometimes, solving a basic, everyday problem is enough.Lessons for other Gen Z entrepreneursCarter Grandbois is one of a growing number of young people who are choosing self-employment over traditional part-time jobs.Here are some lessons based on his experience: Start small and test the idea locally before making a big investment. Use the platforms you’re most comfortable with, especially social media, to market your services. Focus on reliability and customer experience: word of mouth is powerful for local service businesses. Reinvest early profits into better equipment and capacity, but keep costs flexible. For Carter, junk removal is more than a way to make money; it’s a proof of concept that he can build and run a business on his own terms.What’s nextAt 18, Carter is still deciding how far to take the business. He might continue growing it through college, or use it as a financial base while exploring other ventures. Either way, the foundation he has built by 18, equipment, customers, cash flow and a recognisable brand, gives him options many of his peers do not have.From a borrowed trailer at 16 to $15,000 months at 18, Carter Grandbois’s junk-removal business shows that sometimes the most straightforward ideas, executed well and marketed smartly, can turn a teenager’s hustle into a serious enterprise.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1947, Houston opened a 700-plus-seat Art Deco theater; 79 years later, after demolition was planned, supporters raised $2.8 million toward saving the $7.1 million property
articles.summary: US News: For generations of Houston residents, the Garden Oaks Theater was more than a place to watch a movie. Opened in 1947, the Art Deco-style cinema became.
articles.body: For generations of Houston residents, the Garden Oaks Theater was more than a place to watch a movie. Opened in 1947, the Art Deco-style cinema became part of the character of the Garden Oaks and Independence Heights area, eventually serving the community for decades before being converted into a church. Nearly eight decades after its opening, the building found itself facing a very different future. Its new owner had planned to demolish the property, putting one of Houston's remaining historic cinemas at risk. But instead of allowing the theater to disappear, a local preservation campaign brought together residents, donors and filmmakers to try to reclaim the site. According to Arthouse Houston, it had raised more than $2.8 million through its community campaign and was moving forward with plans to purchase the property and transform it into an arts and film center.A theater from 1947The Garden Oaks Theater opened its doors in 1947, during the postwar period when neighbourhood movie theaters were important gathering places across American cities. The cinema seated more than 700 people. Its Art Deco design also gave the building an architectural identity that distinguished it from ordinary commercial properties. According to Arthouse Houston, the theater is one of the few remaining examples of its kind in Houston.The theater continued operating as a cinema until 1997. It was later converted for use by Grace Church, which occupied the building for years before eventually vacating it. Grace Church sold the property in October 2025 to Houston-based Heights Investment Fund for $7.1 million, according to the Houston Chronicle.Demolition becomes a threatThe building's future became uncertain because it did not have landmark protection that would prevent demolition. Concern intensified in February 2026 when crews began removing signage from the property. Preservationists feared Houston could lose another historic cinema at a time when relatively few historic theaters remain. The Garden Oaks Theater was also notable for its surviving architectural details, including its lobby, terrazzo flooring and murals.The prospect of demolition prompted community opposition and eventually brought Arthouse Houston into the effort. The nonprofit had previously emerged from the campaign to preserve Houston's River Oaks Theatre, which reopened in 2024 following restoration efforts.A $7.1 million rescueIn February, Arthouse Houston reached an agreement to purchase the Garden Oaks property for $7.1 million, the same amount the investment fund had paid for it. The organisation then faced a race against time to raise enough money to complete the purchase and prevent demolition. The campaign initially involved a much larger fundraising challenge, but the nonprofit ultimately developed a financing strategy that combined community donations, major pledges and other support. According to Arthouse Houston, it had raised more than $2.8 million toward its immediate $3.1 million fundraising target. That left several hundred thousand dollars still to be raised, although the organisation said it was proceeding into the next phase of its plans. The campaign received significant attention from Houston-raised filmmakers Wes Anderson and Richard Linklater. Anderson participated in a July fundraising event that attracted nearly 500 people and generated approximately $300,000 for the campaign.From cinema to arts hubSaving the building is only the first part of Arthouse Houston's larger plan. The nonprofit envisions turning the former theater into an Arts & Film Center that combines historic preservation with new cultural uses. The proposed project would include screening spaces, production studios, classrooms, a microcinema and flexible performance areas. Plans also call for restoring recognisable elements of the original theater, including its marquee, neon blade sign, grand staircase handrail and murals.The complete project, including acquisition, restoration and equipment, is estimated to cost about $18 million. During renovations, the organisation plans to operate the site as a temporary drive-in theater. A grand opening for the completed center is targeted for 2028.Preserving a piece of HoustonThe Garden Oaks campaign illustrates the challenge facing historic buildings in rapidly changing cities. Once a neighbourhood theater is demolished, its original architecture and the memories attached to it cannot easily be recreated. For Arthouse Houston, the goal is therefore not simply to preserve an old cinema. The proposed center would give the building a new purpose while retaining elements of its history. If the acquisition is completed, the Garden Oaks Theater could once again become a gathering place, this time for movies, live performances, education, filmmaking and community events. After nearly 80 years, the building's story may be shifting from one of impending demolition to one of preservation and reinvention.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Oakland coffee shop accused of kicking out Jewish dad, 5-year-old son and shutters amid antisemitism lawsuits
articles.summary: Jerusalem Coffee House faces a federal civil rights trial after the Justice Department alleged the Oakland cafe refused service to Jewish customers.
articles.body: Jerusalem Coffee House in Oakland, California, remained closed Wednesday after temporarily shutting its doors last week to focus on three lawsuits alleging it discriminated against Jewish customers, including a father and his 5-year-old son. The Palestinian-owned café is preparing for an October federal civil rights trial. The coffeehouse announced in August that it would stop operating after Aug. 23 while its owners prepared for the litigation, including a Justice Department case scheduled for trial Oct. 26. A federal judge previously rejected the defendants’ attempt to dismiss the DOJ lawsuit, which alleges Fathi Abdulrahim Harara and employees refused service to Jewish customers wearing Star of David caps and followed them outside while hurling insults and threats. The café blamed its legal problems on efforts to suppress its pro-Palestinian politics in an August statement on Substack, announcing the closure. DOJ INVESTIGATING NYC COFFEE SHOP OVER HOSTILE SOCIAL POST ABOUT PRO-ISRAEL POLITICIAN "These lawsuits represent the ongoing efforts of Zionist organizations and the federal government to use the courts as a tool to repress free speech and public political commitments to Palestine," it said. Elizabeth Barcohana, the California Republican Party Jewish engagement chair and an attorney, criticized the shop’s defense of its conduct in a statement to Fox News Digital Wednesday. "It is ironic that after freely expressing support for terrorism with these beverage names, the café owners appear to now be using the First Amendment as a defense for ejecting two Jewish customers who wore hats with Stars of David on them, in one case calling it a 'violent' hat," she said. "By their own standard, if a hat can be violent, so can an iced tea. The First Amendment protects speech on hats; it does NOT protect businesses open to the public to discriminate against its customers because they're Jews while chasing them in the street shouting 'Jew' at them. HAMAS, HEZBOLLAH FLAGS FLY AT ANTI-ISRAEL PROTEST MINUTES AFTER MAMDANI CONDEMNS TERROR PLOT AGAINST JEWS "On the one-year anniversary of October 7th, a Palestinian terrorist attack against innocent civilians that killed over 1,200 people and took hundreds of hostages including children and Americans, Jerusalem Coffee Shop in Oakland unveiled a new menu celebrating terrorism. Beverage items named 'Iced in Tea Fada' celebrate Intifada (an Arabic call to violence signifying resistance by any means necessary, including terrorism) and 'Sweet Sinwar' honoring the principal architect behind the attack," she added. The coffee shop co-founder previously denied that "Sweet Sinwar" referred to the Hamas leader and said the menu's Oct. 7 rollout coincided with the business's anniversary rather than the anniversary of the Hamas attack, according to The San Francisco Standard. Barcohana said she hoped the current shutdown would become permanent. FBI NABS 7 FOR ALLEGED 'CAMPAIGN OF VIOLENCE' TO PRESSURE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN, BUSINESSES OVER ISRAEL TIES "The owners have temporarily closed the coffee shop while they defend this discrimination lawsuit against them," she said. "Hopefully it remains permanently closed." The Justice Department filed its case in June 2025 under Title II of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. The Anti-Defamation League and Benesch sued on behalf of Michael Radice, who alleges he was refused service and subjected to antisemitic slurs, while the Louis D. Brandeis Center filed a state lawsuit on behalf of Jonathan Hirsch, who was ejected with his young son after Harara confronted him over his Star of David hat. When the Justice Department announced its case, Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Civil Rights Division said federal public-accommodation laws applied regardless of the business's political views. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "It is illegal, intolerable and reprehensible for any American business open to the public to refuse to serve Jewish customers," she said. "Through our vigorous enforcement of Title II of the Civil Rights Act and other laws prohibiting race and religious discrimination, the Justice Department is committed to combatting antisemitism and discrimination and protecting the civil rights of all Americans."
