articles.body: A young Instagram creator known as michaelshowscoolthings has found himself receiving support from some very big names online after saying he needs to pause his Terraria videos. The creator had been uploading clips of himself playing the game for more than a week. Then, his posting suddenly slowed because his family is moving to another state, leaving him “just really sad” about the situation. The creator’s story has also stood out because of how simple his videos are. Instead of using a complicated recording setup or software such as OBS, he films his screen with a phone while playing Terraria. That basic approach has become part of what makes the clips feel different. Now, with a move forcing him to step away for a few days, creators including MrBeast have stepped in with messages of encouragement.How michaelshowscoolthings built his Terraria followingBefore the break, michaelshowscoolthings had been regularly posting Terraria clips on Instagram. His setup is pretty basic: a phone pointed at the screen while he plays. There is no mention of a big production setup or OBS.That simplicity is actually part of the appeal. His videos show a young creator starting out with what he has, rather than waiting until everything is perfect. It also fits into a much bigger trend where kids are growing up seeing online content creation as a possible career.For some, the dream is to become the next MrBeast, Valkyrae, or Jake Paul. They begin with phones and gradually look toward better equipment and bigger audiences.Why the Terraria creator said he needed to stop postingAfter more than a week of regular uploads, the creator told followers that things in his personal life had become difficult.“I’m gonna be stopping the Terraria videos for a little bit because everything has just been going horrible,” he said.He explained that his family was moving and that he could not continue making Terraria videos during the change. His initial plan was to stop posting them for around four days.The situation appeared to be hitting him emotionally too. In a comment, he said he was “just really sad” about having to move. He then explained that his family was struggling financially enough that they had to move to another state, while his dad wanted to remain in the same state to start his own business.MrBeast and other creators send messages to the young creatorThe announcement did not go unnoticed by larger online personalities. MrBeast, whose real name is Jimmy Donaldson, left a short but encouraging message: “Keep your head up.”YouTuber Agent of Chaos also encouraged him, writing, “Stay with it, king. Things will get better.”Piques offered something more direct. “Hey buddy, keep your head up. Dm ‘e when your new video is up and I will reshare it for you. Never give up on the things you love to do,” he wrote.Activist Patricia Arquette was also among the public figures who offered support.For now, the young creator’s plan is simple: take a short break while his family deals with the move, then return to the Terraria videos he had been posting.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘I first started working when I was broke’: HasanAbi responds to Community Note over his financial past
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Hasan “HasanAbi” Piker has responded after an X Community Note challenged his claim that he was once financially broke. The political commentator said.
articles.body: Hasan “HasanAbi” Piker has responded after an X Community Note challenged his claim that he was once financially broke. The political commentator said critics were ignoring an important part of his financial history. According to HasanAbi, he grew up in an affluent household but his family’s financial situation changed before he entered college. He said there was also a period after college and before he started working when he had little money. HasanAbi pushed back against the criticism and said his current wealth does not conflict with his socialist beliefs.HasanAbi explains why he says he was once brokeThe discussion followed HasanAbi’s recent comments about his financial background. A Community Note on X challenged the way his claim about being broke was being presented.During his stream, HasanAbi argued that people criticizing him were leaving out the period between college and his first job.He said:“I like that throughout my history, throughout my history, okay? There is-throughout my history, there is a moment between college and when I first started working when I was broke. And I’ve explained it all over and over again. And what’s really interesting about this, what’s really interesting about this, is that they just omit that one part of the story to just be like, ‘Yeah, he’s lying, actually.’”HasanAbi also addressed his current financial position. He said he is proud that he can financially support his parents and does not see that as something that conflicts with his political views.“I take care of my family. I’m very proud that I am fortunate enough to be able to take care of my family. Neither my mom nor my dad work anymore. I take care of them financially, and I am fortunate to be able to do so. It doesn’t really matter. These guys are ****ing insane.”He later clarified that he does not deny growing up with financial privilege.“And yes, I did grow up affluent. I could easily lie about it. Why would I? There’s no reason to. By the time I got to college, my dad lost all of his money.”HasanAbi’s comments are consistent with his broader argument that his childhood circumstances and his later financial success should not be reduced to a single description of his background. A recent transcript of his appearance on The Breakfast Club also shows him discussing criticism over being a wealthy socialist and arguing that personal wealth does not automatically contradict his political beliefs.HasanAbi says socialism is not a “poverty cult”HasanAbi also connected the discussion to the criticism he often receives over his socialist views and his wealth.He argued that socialism is not based on everyone having the same amount of money or living in poverty. Instead, he said his goal is for people from different financial backgrounds to support the same economic system.“We want everyone to be socialists. Socialism is not a poverty cult. It’s not a vow to poverty, okay? Which is ironically what I was talking about in that video as well on The Breakfast Club. We want everyone to be a socialist, okay? We want rich people to be socialists. We want poor people to be socialists. There is no—there is no contradiction here.”HasanAbi has made similar comments before. In a recent The Breakfast Club appearance, he argued that socialism does not mean giving up comfort or refusing to enjoy things. He said the idea is about creating a society where everyone can live comfortably rather than making everyone equally poor.The latest discussion has once again brought attention to HasanAbi’s financial background and his position as a wealthy streamer who openly identifies as a socialist. His response focused on what he described as missing context around his years between college and employment, while also acknowledging that he grew up affluent.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: EU pursuing more Russia sanctions after failed airport attack: Kallas
articles.summary: EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas warns of more pressure after Germany blames Russia for attempted attack.
articles.body:
European Union foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas has said the bloc is ramping up pressure on Russia after Berlin accused Moscow of being behind a failed drone attack on a German airport.

Kallas struck a defiant tone on Wednesday as she warned that “attempts to intimidate Europe” would fail. She further denounced last month’s attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport as “state-sponsored terrorism”.

“We ⁠are working on new proposals to tighten sanctions enforcement and we are moving ahead with more sanctions,” Kallas said.

Russia has denied involvement in the incident, with President Vladimir Putin alleging that the evidence had been “planted”. Three drones carrying explosives were found in and around the airport on August 4, temporarily disrupting air traffic.

In a post on X on Wednesday, Kallas said the bloc was preparing to sanction an additional 1,600 individuals and entities linked to Russia’s military sector and that the EU was “ready to add more”.

Kallas also highlighted broad support among the bloc’s foreign ministers for imposing a ban on former Russian military personnel from visiting the EU, while also floating the prospect of tightening visa restrictions for Russian tourists.

She added that Russia’s representative to the bloc had been summoned by the EU and individual member states.

The EU has attempted to apply as much pressure on Russia as possible without resorting to military means. To date, more than 3,000 Russian officials, oligarchs and companies have already been sanctioned since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Wednesday that authorities were looking into how “to cut deeper into Russia’s war chest”.

She said the attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport marked “a new escalation on European Union soil”.

It was not clear what, if any, effect further measures by the EU will have on Russia in terms of the Ukraine conflict, which has largely become a war of attrition.

Kyiv has repeatedly targeted energy infrastructure deep in Russian territory, while Moscow has taken advantage of Ukraine’s lack of missile interceptors by carrying out regular strikes that have killed civilians.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has said Russia would have to live with the consequences of its actions, warning that a response had been carefully prepared.

Russia’s foreign ministry, meanwhile, said it had summoned Germany’s envoy to the country, Bernd Finke, telling him that Moscow “categorically” rejected being behind the failed drone attack.

articles.title: Malta businessman acquitted of plotting journalist Caruana Galizia murder
articles.summary: The 2017 killing of anticorruption journalist shocked Europe and set off a political firestorm in Malta.
articles.body:
A court in Malta has acquitted businessman Yorgen Fenech of masterminding the murder of prominent anticorruption journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia.

Fenech, 44, was acquitted on Wednesday at the end of a jury trial. He had been tried on charges of complicity to murder and for the lesser charge of criminal association to commit murder.

If found guilty, Fenech could have faced life in prison.

Caruana Galizia’s family were seen weeping in the packed courtroom in Valletta after the businessman was cleared of both counts by an 8-1 margin following eight hours of deliberation by the jury.

“Nine years after Daphne’s brutal assassination, the institutional failures that enabled her murder remain unaddressed and unreformed,” the slain reporter’s family said in a statement.

“Lasting justice means no person should ever face the same risks again. Our country failed to protect Daphne’s life. It owes it to her to prevent other lives being lost.”

Fenech’s family members were seen celebrating the jury’s decision.

The killing of Caruana Galizia in October 2017 shocked Europe’s journalist community and set off a political firestorm in Malta, focusing international attention on its police and judiciary.

Dubbed a “one-woman WikiLeaks”, Caruana Galizia had exposed corruption at the highest level in the Mediterranean island country, shining a spotlight on links between Malta’s business and political elites. She was 53 when she was killed.

Prosecutors argued that Fenech had wanted Caruana Galizia killed because she was about to reveal information about him.

Fenech has denied the accusations. His defence instead pointed fingers at his one-time friend Keith Schembri, the former chief of staff of then-Prime Minister Joseph Muscat and a target of Caruana Galizia’s blogs.

Muscat, who was never linked to the murder, stepped down in January 2020 due to the political fallout from the assassination.

Police told the court that Schembri had never been a suspect. He has denied any role in the murder.

An independent inquiry in 2021 found that officials in Malta had failed to protect Caruana Galizia from threats to her life before her death.

articles.title: What is a Tuey-Rodriguez charge? Judge gives instruction to deadlocked Lindsay Clancy jury
articles.summary: The judge in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial issued a rare Tuey-Rodriguez charge after jurors again said they were deadlocked. Learn what the Massachusetts jury instruction is.
articles.body: A Massachusetts judge overseeing the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy gave jurors a Tuey-Rodriguez charge Wednesday after they reported for a second time that they were unable to reach a unanimous verdict. The instruction is given to a deadlocked jury to encourage continued deliberations while reminding jurors they should not abandon honestly held beliefs simply to reach a verdict. Judge William Sullivan sent jurors back to deliberate Tuesday after they first indicated they were struggling to agree. After the jury again reported that it was deadlocked, Sullivan delivered the formal charge. A Tuey-Rodriguez charge is unique to Massachusetts and is sometimes called a "dynamite charge" because it is intended to help break a jury impasse without coercing a verdict. LINDSAY CLANCY VERDICT STILL WITHIN REACH – RETIRED MASSACHUSETTS JUDGE PUSHES BACK ON HUNG-JURY PREDICTIONS The instruction takes its name from two Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court decisions. In Commonwealth v. Tuey (1851), the court approved an instruction encouraging deadlocked jurors to re-examine their views with an open mind. More than a century later, in Commonwealth v. Rodriguez (1973), the state's highest court revised that language to remove pressure on minority or holdout jurors, creating a neutral instruction that asks all jurors to carefully consider one another's views while maintaining their own honestly held convictions. Receiving a Tuey-Rodriguez charge does not mean a verdict is imminent. The instruction is generally considered a necessary step before a judge declares a mistrial because of a hung jury, although it often results in jurors reaching a unanimous verdict after further deliberations. LINDSAY CLANCY’S FUTURE COULD REST WITH ‘PROSECUTION DOCTORS’ AS CASE ECHOES INFAMOUS MAINE KILLINGS: EXPERT Retired Massachusetts Superior Court Judge Thomas Drechsler told Fox News Digital the instruction is typically given only after a judge determines jurors have fully deliberated but remain deadlocked. "The charge encourages the jurors to rethink their own feelings in light of what other jurors feel" while reminding them that no one is in a better position to decide the case than the jurors who heard all the evidence, Drechsler said. If jurors report they remain deadlocked after receiving the instruction, "there's a higher likelihood" the case could end in a mistrial, Drechsler said, though he noted he has seen juries return verdicts after receiving a Tuey-Rodriguez charge. Clancy faces three counts of first-degree murder in the January 2023 deaths of her three children — Cora, Dawson and Callan — at the family's Duxbury, Massachusetts, home. She does not dispute killing the children but argues she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and was not criminally responsible at the time. Prosecutors contend Clancy was legally sane and intentionally planned the killings. If they remain unable to reach a unanimous verdict, Sullivan could declare a mistrial, leaving prosecutors to decide whether to seek a new trial.

Saudi Arabia has condemned an Iranian attack on an oil tanker owned by its national shipping company that resulted in the deaths of two citizens of the Philippines.

Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry on Wednesday said Iran targeted the Sidr tanker, owned by national carrier Bahri, while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz two days earlier.

“The kingdom stressed the necessity of halting escalations, and respecting international maritime safety and the security of global energy supplies,” the Saudi foreign ministry said in a statement.

Saudi Arabia’s regional neighbours also condemned the attack, one of several recent incidents in the US-Israeli war with Iran launched on February 28.

Kuwait and Qatar’s foreign ministries said the attack violated international law and freedom of maritime navigation.

Qatar called the attack a “flagrant violation of the rules of international law and freedom of maritime navigation”. Doha further rejected the use of the Strait of Hormuz as a “bargaining chip”.

Bahri, meanwhile, also confirmed the death on social media.

“Bahri confirms that its vessel SIDR was involved in a security incident while transiting the Strait of Hormuz” late on Monday, it said.

“Bahri remains in continuous contact with the vessel and is coordinating closely with the relevant authorities and maritime industry stakeholders, while continuing to closely monitor developments,” it said.

Iran has repeatedly attacked and threatened tankers attempting to sail through the strategic waterway without authorisation, impeding energy exports from neighbouring oil-rich Gulf countries.

The US has maintained that vessels can safely transit the waterway, through which traffic has slowed considerably . Washington has promised to continue its counter-blockade of Iranian ports indefinitely.

Overnight Monday into Tuesday, unidentified projectiles struck two oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Greek maritime risk management firm Marisks had said.

Both vessels loaded two million barrels of crude at Juaymah on Saudi Arabia’s east coast last week, according to Kpler data.

On Wednesday, Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said two oil tankers caught fire after striking mines while transiting the strait.

Before the US-Israel war with Iran began, about 20 percent of the world’s oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz.

In July, another Bahri vessel, the Wedyan supertanker, was hit while passing through the strait close to Oman’s coast.

Two other Bahri vessels, Masa and Amzan, were attacked in the Red Sea in July and August after Yemen’s Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: In 2018, California Governor Gavin Newsom bought a $3.7 million Fair Oaks mansion; now he lists the 8.2-acre estate for $7.5 million with 7 bedrooms, 12 baths and luxury amenities
articles.summary: US News: California Governor Gavin Newsom has put his sprawling Sacramento-area mansion on the market for $7.5 million, months before his second term comes to .
articles.body: California Governor Gavin Newsom has put his sprawling Sacramento-area mansion on the market for $7.5 million, months before his second term comes to an end in January 2027. The Spanish-style estate in Fair Oaks features seven bedrooms, 12 bathrooms and a host of luxury amenities, including a tennis court, swimming pool and a 5,000-bottle wine cellar.The 8.2-acre property, located in an exclusive enclave near the American River, was listed on Monday by Sotheby’s International Realty agents Matthew Hindy and Nick Sadek. Newsom reportedly paid $3.7 million for the home in late 2018, shortly after winning his first term as California governor.Spread across roughly 12,600 square feet, the Santa Barbara-inspired residence is set beyond a gated driveway and features beige stucco walls and a terracotta roof.Inside, the home includes a grand entry foyer with high ceilings and exposed wood beams, a fireside living room with sliding glass doors, a wet bar, formal dining room and a bright kitchen with an eat-in island and butler’s pantry. The property also has a breakfast nook and family room.Luxury amenities include wine cellar and wellness areaThe mansion's secluded primary suite includes dual walk-in closets and a spacious bathroom with two showers, two water closets and a travertine soaking tub. An outdoor wellness area features a cold plunge pool and hot tub.Other amenities include a study lined with bookshelves, a game room, gym, 5,000-bottle wine cellar and a separate guest casita with its own kitchen. The landscaped grounds feature a swimming pool and full-size tennis court.Newsom and his family previously called it homeNewsom and his wife, Jennifer Siebel Newsom, moved into the Fair Oaks property in 2019 after briefly living at California's historic governor's mansion in Sacramento. At the time, a spokesperson described the Fair Oaks estate as being “more kid-friendly”, according to the Sacramento Bee.The family has since divided its time between Sacramento and Marin County, where they own another property. In 2024, the Newsoms enrolled their children in Marin County schools.The Fair Oaks residence has also been the backdrop to several political moments. In 2020, protesters chained themselves to the property's fence to demonstrate against rising deaths in California prisons during the coronavirus pandemic.The mansion later drew attention in 2024 when Newsom hosted a political fundraiser there for Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, who was campaigning at the time as the Democratic vice-presidential candidate.Presidential ambitions add to speculation around saleNewsom is openly considering a bid for the Democratic presidential nomination in 2028. His decision to sell the Fair Oaks property comes as he prepares to leave the governor's office in January 2027 after two terms.The Newsoms are now transitioning back toward the Bay Area, with the governor's political future likely to remain a focus as speculation builds around a potential 2028 presidential campaign.Newsom bought the house for $3.7 million in 2018 and is now asking $7.5 million for it. If he gets that price, he would make $3.8 million more than what he paid.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: McDonald's brings back popular item for short time as one state gets a treat
articles.summary: Spicy Chicken McNuggets and Mighty Hot Sauce are back at McDonald's for a limited time, while a Texas Meal with collectible cups sparks calls for more states.
articles.body: McDonald's is turning up the heat at participating locations nationwide with the return of Spicy Chicken McNuggets and Mighty Hot Sauce for a limited time. articles.title: Dreams shattered: Gaza amputees struggle under blockade and rubble
articles.summary: Young amputees in Gaza face harsh realities, awaiting prosthetics and battling mobility hurdles.
articles.body:
Gaza City, Gaza Strip – Before Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, 24-year-old Shurouq Khaira was an athlete, training regularly for her track races.

Athletics wasn’t just a hobby for her; it was a core part of her identity. She competed in youth championships, taking a national title in 2016. Her dream was to represent her country, Palestine, on the international stage.

“I wanted the whole world to know that people in Gaza live, dream, strive, and achieve,” she said. “I dreamed of competing in the Olympics.”

The future Shurouq envisioned was shattered on November 19, 2023 – just over a month into a war that is now approaching its three-year anniversary, with Israel killing more than 73,400 Palestinians.

Gaza City was the target of fierce Israeli attacks in those opening weeks of the war, and Shurouq woke up to the sound of shelling targeting her family’s home in the city’s Daraj neighbourhood. One shell hit the house.

Shurouq survived, but her injuries were so severe that doctors were forced to amputate her right leg below the knee. Her father, who had inspired her love for athletics, had both his legs amputated.

Following the shock of the injury, Shurouq’s life turned into a continuous daily struggle to perform the simplest tasks.

Inside the tent her family is forced to live in because of the destruction of their home and Israel’s refusal to allow proper reconstruction in Gaza , nights are particularly difficult. With no light available and the difficulty of using crutches in the dark, she feels stuck, afraid that she will trip and fall on her face.

Outside the tent, movement among streets that largely consist of sand and rubble is difficult, forcing her to hop on one leg to reach her destination.

“I live between pain, fear, darkness, and suffering, but my heart remains patient,” Shurouq said. “This difficulty in movement will be permanent. No matter what prosthetic I get, the feeling of loss will stay with me. It affects me deeply. At times, I feel weak and cry. But there are no solutions, so I try to adapt to this painful reality.”

Shurouq is hoping to get a prosthetic leg, which would make walking easier, but is still waiting. In the meantime, she has to regularly attend physical therapy appointments at various hospitals in Gaza, posing another challenge.

With the little transportation available in Gaza prohibitively expensive, Shurouq is forced to walk for kilometres on one leg. Sometimes she ends up being too late and missing her appointments.

“Everything in Gaza has become extremely difficult, almost impossible,” she said.

Israel’s indiscriminate bombing of Gaza, and the resulting decimated healthcare system in the Palestinian enclave, has led to around 6,000 amputations since the war began, according to the Gaza Ministry of Health.

Around a quarter of the cases are children, making the war in Gaza the largest source of child amputees in modern history, according to the United Nations.

Orthopaedic surgeons in Gaza say that many of the amputation cases could have been avoided, but that the collapse of the Gaza Strip’s hospitals and the depletion of surgical supplies, antiseptics, and anaesthetics has often forced medical teams to resort to amputation as the fastest option to save lives and prevent gangrene.

Those shortages are largely the result of Israel’s restrictions on imports into Gaza, which it maintains despite an October 2025 ceasefire.

In addition to those supplies, there are also restrictions on the import of items that are vital in the production of prosthetics, causing the delays that amputees like Shurouq are suffering from.

Israel imposes strict controls on the importation of items, some of which are so-called “dual-use”, in the sense that Israel deems them to be used for military as well as civilian purposes. This includes silicone, thermoplastics, medical plasters, and mechanical joints.

And there is also a shortage of prosthetists, fitting specialists, and rehabilitation physicians.

The specialists who are still practicing in Gaza have attempted to find alternative solutions, assembling improvised prosthetics and crutches using plastic pipes, wood, and aluminium retrieved from under destroyed buildings.

But Jamal Kallab, a prosthetics and rehabilitation specialist in Gaza, explained that these were not proper replacements for the missing materials.

“These improvised devices are not designed according to the body’s specific needs,” Kallab said. “This leaves them incapable of providing the required support and balance, causing an uneven weight distribution that strains [other body parts].”

Kallab warned that an ill-fitting socket leads to “continuous friction and swelling, followed by severe surgical inflammatory ulcers that stop the limb from being used for long periods”.

Aside from a lack of materials, the sheer number of amputees and the absence of sufficient facilities have led to patients often facing a delay in the start of their rehabilitation programs.

This, according to physical therapist Bissan Kloub, leads to severe weakness and atrophy in the muscles surrounding the amputation site, joint stiffness, a reduced range of motion, and skin swelling that prevents wound healing.

Kloub explained that delays in starting rehabilitation impair walking and cause issues such as incorrect joint postures, “weakening balance and directly affecting the future efficiency of using the prosthetic limb”.

She highlighted the importance of injury rehabilitation to a patient’s wellbeing, referring to the harsh environment in Gaza where a lack of mobility can be severely restricting, and the challenges to the mental health of a young person in particular.

“The challenge is deeper among youth and children because amputation touches their self-image and their relationship with society, requiring comprehensive physical, psychological, and social rehabilitation,” Kloub said.

The issues raised by Kloub are not foreign to 18-year-old Shireen Abu al-Qumsan, who was severely injured in an Israeli attack in May 2025 that led to the amputation of both of her legs.

She continues to wait for prosthetic legs and treatment abroad that requires approval from Israel. For now, she relies on a manual wheelchair for long-distance mobility.

From the home in central Gaza’s Bureij that she lives in with her surviving family – her brother was killed in a separate attack in June 2024 – she explained how difficult it was to travel.

“Moving around in a wheelchair is extremely exhausting,” Shireen said. “The streets of Gaza are completely destroyed, making it more difficult for a wheelchair to pass through.”

She is forced to rely on a companion whenever she leaves the house, and has a strong desire to be self-reliant inside it – not wanting to seem like a burden – but that requires double the effort to do things by herself.

For Shireen, as well as Shurouq, the mental challenge of living with amputated limbs in Gaza is bitter.

Shireen remembers the time her wheelchair flipped over in the street, her mind flashing back to the explosion that took her legs as she fell to the floor, helpless.

Shurouq, meanwhile, is fearful that without a proper prosthetic and rehabilitation, her injury will worsen, or that she will be attacked and injured again.

“I go to sleep curled into myself out of sheer terror,” Shurouq said. “I am constantly afraid another shell will hit us and take the rest of my leg or my arm. The sense of total insecurity makes me sleep clutching my body together from sorrow and pain.”

articles.title: India pledges help to rebuild school in flood-ravaged Nepal
articles.summary: India News: TRISHULI BAZAAR (NUWAKOT, NEPAL): India assured support for complete reconstruction of flood-ravaged Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Bidur, two.
articles.body: TRISHULI BAZAAR (NUWAKOT, NEPAL): India assured support for complete reconstruction of flood-ravaged Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Bidur, two days after TOI reported that the institution was seeking New Delhi's help to rebuild on higher, safer ground.The assurance came less than a week after around 900 students on campus escaped the Aug 26 flash flood following an emergency evacuation, while hundreds more travelling to school were stopped from entering the danger zone. The school had 1,643 students enrolled.Indian ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava met the school's principal Rajendra Dawadi Tuesday. Srivastava recalled the institution's long association with India, including construction of its newer building through Indian grant assistance. He said Dawadi's timely action had saved lives of over 1,600 schoolchildren. TOI had earlier reported how around 900 students were inside the school when warnings came, while buses carrying hundreds of others were stopped before reaching the danger zone.Dawadi told TOI after the meeting with Srivastava on Wednesday: "We are deeply grateful to India for the reassurance and for standing with us at this difficult time. The assurance has given the entire school community hope at a time when we are trying to restart classes and also looking for a safe location for a permanent campus. Our entire school infrastructure has been destroyed, so our immediate priority is to bring the students back to classrooms."The flood has swept away virtually the entire campus, including its 18-room, three-storey academic block. The school's two buses were among the few assets left. Two staffers - non-teaching employee Chulrim Lama and secondary teacher Santos Parihar - still remain missing.The school's links with India stretch back decades. Embassy of India records said Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School was established in 1951 and was designed by K I Singh, an Indian engineer who had come to Nepal for Trishuli Hydro Project. India later funded a new school building at a cost of NRs 25 million, or Nepalese Rs 2.5 crore, under India-Nepal Development Cooperation. Indian officials and local authorities inaugurated the building on Aug 2, 2022.India's latest assurance came as Nepal's private sector also mobilised assistance for schools and communities hit by the flood. Chaudhary Foundation, CSR arm of Chaudhary Group, announced immediate assistance to help Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School restart classes from a temporary location.Dawadi said restoring a Bailey bridge would make restart easier. He said bringing children back together with their classmates and teachers would help them recover from trauma.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Reports: German investigators identify two suspects in drone attack
articles.summary: German investigators are looking into two suspects in relation to the failed drone attack at Leipzig airport last month that Berlin believes was carried out...
articles.body:
German investigators are looking into two suspects in relation to the failed drone attack at Leipzig airport believed to be carried out on behalf of Russia.

Italy intends to investigate reports that one of the suspects entered the EU on an Italian tourist visa issued in Belarus, sparking discussions about possible tightening of visa rules at an EU foreign ministers' meeting.

The incident at Leipzig airport has reignited debates within the EU about visa rules for people from Russia and partner states, with concerns raised about the potential security risks posed by the current visa issuance practices.

German investigators are looking into two suspects in relation to the failed drone attack at Leipzig airport last month that Berlin believes was carried out on behalf of Russia, several German media outlets reported on Wednesday.

Die Zeit weekly reported that federal prosecutors are investigating two suspects.

Broadcasters NDR and WDR as well as the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper reported that federal criminal police have identified two suspects.

The Federal Public Prosecutor's Office declined to comment on the reports.

It comes a day after Germany officially blamed Russia for an explosive-laden drone that was discovered near Ukrainian cargo aircraft at the eastern German airport on the evening of August 4.

Moscow denies any involvement with the drone and has described the incident involving the device, which failed to detonate, as a "provocation" serving the interests of militaristic circles in Europe and Ukraine.

Meanwhile, Italy intends to investigate reports that a person believed to be involved in the alleged Russian attempted attack at Leipzig airport is said to have entered the EU on a tourist visa issued by Italy.

All necessary investigations would now be carried out, Italian Foreign Minister, Antonio Tajani said on the sidelines of an EU meeting in Ireland.

In principle, he explained, there is a procedure for issuing visas and certain requirements must be met. If the individuals in question meet these requirements and there are no alerts on record concerning them, the visa is issued.

According to research by NDR, WDR and Süddeutsche Zeitung, one of them is said to have entered the Schengen Area on an Italian tourist visa. According to the authorities' findings, the document was issued at the end of April at an Italian diplomatic mission in Minsk, the capital of Belarus.

At the EU foreign ministers' meeting in Ireland, the reports sparked fresh discussions about a possible tightening of visa rules. If it were true that one of the suspects had travelled to the EU on an Italian tourist visa, this would demonstrate very clearly that the EU could be harmed through the use of visas, EU chief diplomat Kaja Kallas said.

Many member states had already pointed out in the past that such tourist visas were being used for acts of sabotage because the perpetrators needed to gain entry to the European Union. She hoped that, should the information be confirmed, the current visa restrictions could be tightened. "Because this is actually also about our own security," she said.

Since the start of Russia's war against Ukraine, there have been repeated discussions within the EU about visa rules for people from Russia and partner states such as Belarus.

These rules have already been tightened on several occasions, but they still allow EU member states to issue numerous visas to tourists from those countries.

For example, Italian, French and Spanish consulates in Russia have recently continued to issue a six-figure number of Schengen visas. Critics accuse these countries of being unwilling to turn away wealthy tourists.

articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Centre is likely to come up with a \"social media code of conduct\" for its officers, a first such move amid a growing trend among them posti.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Centre is likely to come up with a "social media code of conduct" for its officers, a first such move amid a growing trend among them posting personal reels, videos, stories and opinions, some while on duty. PM Modi has directed top bureaucrats to explore the possibility of bringing out the code.During a recent interaction with secretaries, he also asked ministry of electronics and IT to expedite rollout of "Ek Bharat" portal, a unified service delivery platform for citizens.TOI has learnt that cabinet secretary T V Somanathan, in a communication to bureaucrats this week, has outlined the action points emerging from the meeting.The proposal for the social media code is significant, as in many cases, officers through social media posts glorify their work and position - acts inconsistent with the expected conduct of govt employees.Some senior serving and retired officials said there is a dire need for this, considering there is no such code at present, except conduct rules, which were framed at a time when there was no social media and, hence, don't contain specific provisions for this.The need for "Ek Bharat portal" has been felt considering citizens need to log into multiple websites for availing govt services and remember usernames and passwords. Once operational, users need just one username and password to access all govt portals for services. Officials said a few rounds of meetings have been held among departments.As per Somanathan's communication, PM has also asked secretaries to work for collective goals as part of the "whole of govt" approach rather than defending narrow departmental interests.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: '23 Silkyara 'rat miners' offer to join Nepal tunnel rescue
articles.summary: India News: A Delhi-NCR team of \"rat miners\", whose manual excavation helped rescue all 41 workers trapped in Silkyara tunnel in 2023, has offered to join rescue .
articles.body: A Delhi-NCR team of "rat miners", whose manual excavation helped rescue all 41 workers trapped in Silkyara tunnel in 2023, has offered to join rescue operations in flood-hit Nepal, where at least 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects and about 500 are believed to be inside tunnels. Nepal Army has been prioritising search and rescue operations in 19 hydropower tunnels.Anand Kansal, Pune-based volunteer coordinator for the team, has written to Indian ambassador to Nepal, seeking help in placing the miners' expertise at the disposal of Nepalese authorities."We were highly moved after seeing news and videos (of the floods)... this is one of the worst tragedies we've witnessed in recent times," he said.Floods have damaged at least 12 hydropower projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot - four under construction, seven operational and one undergoing testing - with mud, boulders and debris blocking or collapsing sections of tunnels.The miners came into national prominence during the Nov 2023 Silkyara-Bend-Barkot tunnel operation after mechanical drilling repeatedly failed. They entered a narrow rescue pipe and manually excavated the final stretch through the debris, helping rescuers reach 41 workers after 17 days underground.A 12-member team of the miners was also deployed at the Srisailam Left Bank Canal tunnel in Telangana in Feb 2025 after a collapse trapped eight workers. They worked there alongside specialised rescue agencies in difficult, debris-filled conditions.Firoz Qureshi, who took part in the Silkyara rescue, said the team was ready to leave immediately if Nepal sought its help. "We know what those families are going through right now, waiting for word. If we can go and help, we are ready today, not tomorrow."Monu Kumar, the youngest member of the group, said their manual techniques could be useful where heavy machinery was unable to penetrate. "Our hands and our tools can go where big machines cannot," he said. "We just need permission to go and start."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: India News: GUWAHATI: Two Kuki-Zo MLAs travelled to Imphal Wednesday in defiance of a community whip and attended the Manipur assembly session in person for the f.
articles.body: GUWAHATI: Two Kuki-Zo MLAs travelled to Imphal Wednesday in defiance of a community whip and attended the Manipur assembly session in person for the first time since violence erupted in 2023, creating a hill-valley divide that is still to be bridged.Saikul legislator Kimneo Haokip Hangshing of Kuki Peoples' Alliance (KPA) and Independent MLA Haokholet Kipgen of Saitu, both in Kangpokpi district, chose to be in the assembly for the first day of the session despite Kuki Inpi Manipur's explicit instruction to stay away from Meitei-majority Imphal.Deputy CM Nemcha Kipgen and her BJP colleague, Henglep MLA Letzamang Haokip, attended the session over videoconferencing. Other four Kuki-Zo MLAs from BJP abstained. Manipur has nine Kuki-Zo MLAs, including two from KPA. Six of them had attended the budget session last Feb virtually.CM Y Khemchand Singh's office issued a statement lauding the two Kuki MLAs for making what it termed a "historic physical return" to the assembly. "Their attendance comes after a gap of three and a half years, during which representatives from the community had not physically participated in person in House proceedings," it said.Singh attributed the MLA duo's "positive step" to BJP-led govt's efforts to reduce the trust deficit among communities. "With collective efforts, Manipur can strive to walk the path to peace," Singh said.Kuki Inpi Manipur has barred elected community representatives from venturing into Imphal Valley until Union and state govts accede to their demand for a separate administration for the hills.While violence involving Kuki and Meitei communities has ebbed, Manipur is firefighting escalating tensions between Naga and Kuki groups in the hills, mainly along the Imphal-Tamenglong Road corridor in Kangpokpi. articles.title: What you need to know: US launches coin featuring Trump’s face
articles.summary: The coin marks the first time in nearly 200 years that a living person has been featured on the country’s currency.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump’s face has officially found its way onto the country’s currency.

On Tuesday at 12pm Eastern Time (16:00 GMT), the US Mint began circulating – and selling – a “once-in-a-generation” $1 coin bearing Trump’s likeness to commemorate the nation’s 250th anniversary.

The gold-coloured coins feature Trump’s portrait on one side, alongside inscriptions of “LIBERTY” and “IN GOD WE TRUST”. On the reverse is an illustration of the US presidential seal with “250” inscribed on its shield.

The US Mint says the coins “capture the spirit, pride, and legacy of a nation approaching its landmark anniversary”.

It’s the first time in nearly 100 years that a living person has been featured on US currency, drawing a heavy dose of criticism, since such honours are largely reserved for long-dead dignitaries.

How did this $1 coin come to be? Here’s what you need to know:

Since Trump returned to the White House last year, the administration has taken steps to put his name or image on an array of buildings and items, including the Kennedy Center , the US Institute of Peace, National Parks passes, a limited-edition passport and a $1m “gold card” visa that was announced last year.

The Trump administration has tied some of those efforts to celebrations of the country’s semiquincentennial, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.

On July 15, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent first announced the coin in a post on social media. Bessent said the coin “celebrates the strength of American values, and the promise of a nation dedicated to preserving freedom for all”.

The Trump administration has also pointed to another anniversary coin as a precedent for the Trump-branded $1 piece.

In 1926, for the 150th anniversary of the country, the US Mint struck a coin featuring side-by-side portraits of George Washington and Calvin Coolidge, a president who was in office at the time.

But critics have pointed out that the 1926 coin was commemorative and not intended for circulation as currency.

Are there other proposals for Trump-themed currency?

In May, Bessent also said preparations were under way to print a new $250 banknote featuring Trump’s face.

Bessent added that the Trump administration was seeking congressional approval for the new bill.

Despite the coin being valued at $1, consumers can purchase a 25-coin roll for $61 or a 100-coin bag for $154.50 — a significant mark-up.

While the coins are being sold at a premium, the US Mint emphasises they are not solely decorative.

They are valid currency and can be used to make everyday purchases, just like a $1 bill.

US federal law states: “Only the portrait of a deceased individual may appear on United States currency and securities.”

Congress passed that law in 1866 after a Department of the Treasury official, Spencer M Clark, put his own face on a note valued at five cents, angering lawmakers.

However, during his first term, Trump signed legislation known as the Circulating Collection Coin Redesign Act of 2020 (CCRA), which gave the Treasury the authority to mint $1 coins “with designs emblematic of the United States semiquincentennial”.

That law prohibits the portrait of “any person, living or dead” on the reverse side of those coins. However, Trump’s image on the new $1 coin appears on the obverse — the front of the coin — meaning it likely complies with the law.

Late last year, Democratic Senators Catherine Cortez Masto of Nevada and Jeff Merkley of Oregon introduced legislation that would block Trump from placing his face on the coin.

“While monarchs put their faces on coins, America has never had and never will have a king,” Cortez Masto said. “Our legislation would codify this country’s long-standing tradition of not putting living Presidents on American coins. Congress must pass it without delay.” Their bill did not become law.

The Treasury Department and US Mint did not immediately respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

articles.summary: US News: 20-year-old Pierre Damas Bel in Ohio got out of his car and stepped into the traffic on Ohio State Highway after a brief conversation with his father..
articles.body: 20-year-old Pierre Damas Bel in Ohio got out of his car and stepped into the traffic on Ohio State Highway after a brief conversation with his father. The freshman student at Wright State University told his father that he was not OK because he was being bullied, as he had an ankle monitor issued by ICE in July. The Haitian family came to the US legally in 2024 under the Temporary Protected Status which has now been removed, with thousands of Haitians navigating the same misery.Pierre Damas Bel was an avid soccer player, but he was not able to play soccer and did not even get a new ROTC uniform, for which he was being bullied. On Monday, his father, Pierre Ronal Bel got a video call from his distressed son. He asked him to come home. But instead, cops showed up at his door and informed him that Damas had thrown himself under a truck and was killed. Family members said it was a suicide, while the investigation remains open.ICE said the family applied for admission in Texas in March 2024 and the Biden administration released them inside the country. ICE did not take the blame of the suicide on their oppression. “ICE does not comment on the cause of death while that investigation is pending, and we will not speculate about unverified claims regarding other individuals,” a spokesperson said adding that undocumented people always have the chance to self-deport.“Remaining in the country illegally, while fighting removal, is a choice. Leaving with a free flight home and $2,600 is also a choice,” the spokesperson said. “ICE will continue to use detention or alternatives to detention as needed (for) those illegal aliens who stay in violation of the law.”Wright State University issued a statement in which they said: “The safety and well-being of our students is the highest priority, and we remain dedicated to providing a campus community where every student feels safe, supported, included and welcomed".'I came here to pursue my education'In recent social media posts, Bel described his frustration with the ankle monitor. “I came to this country to pursue my education. I didn’t come here to commit a crime or hurt anyone. Yet now I’m walking through the streets of the United States with a GPS monitor on my leg, carrying a feeling of shame and humiliation that I never imagined I would experience,” he wrote in a July 30 Instagram post. “I came here to study, to build my future, and to live a better (life) not to be treated like criminal. So now, how am I supposed play college sports with a GPS monitor on my leg?”This article mentions suicide. If you feel you are in crisis, call or text 988Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump suggests renaming Strait of Hormuz as Trump Strait amid Iran war
articles.summary: Despite renewed fighting with Iran and near daily attacks on ships, Trump says Strait of Hormuz is ‘under USA control’.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz after himself, reasserting that the waterway is under Washington’s control despite near-daily Iranian attacks on ships in the area.

Trump’s suggestion on Wednesday came less than 24 hours after the US struck several targets in Iran, killing at least four people, including two children , at a wedding in the southern city of Sirik.

“Now that we have it under USA control, should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT???” Trump wrote in a social media post.

“Like America itself, it would be ‘hotter’ than ever before!”

Iran responded to Tuesday’s attack with missile launches against US bases in the region. The fighting pushed oil prices upwards by around 4 percent.

Despite repeated claims by US officials that the Strait of Hormuz is now open and millions of barrels of oil are transiting through it daily, oil prices have not fallen in recent weeks.

Iran continues to maintain that the waterway is closed and under its control.

On Wednesday, Saudi Arabia accused Iran of carrying out a strike on an oil tanker that killed two people.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), a monitoring agency affiliated with the British Royal Navy, has been reporting attacks on vessels in Hormuz almost every day.

In the US, the price of petrol is rising. It reached $4.12 per gallon (3.8 litres) on Wednesday, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA), up from less than $3 before the war started on February 28.

When Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu started the conflict by attacking Iran and killing its supreme leader earlier this year, the US president promised that the war would last for six weeks.

But the promised quick end to what Trump initially dubbed a “little excursion” never materialised. The conflict entered its seventh month last week.

Still, Trump has continued to claim victory and control over Hormuz, repeatedly claiming that Iran has been defeated militarily despite its ability to strike back against US interests in the region.

After the US strikes on Tuesday, Trump sternly warned Tehran against retaliating, saying that Iran would be “hit again at a much harder and higher level” if it responds.

But within hours, Iran’s military fired missiles and drones at US bases in Bahrain, Jordan and Iraq.

The “Trump Strait” suggestion on Wednesday is the latest push by the US president to assert control over a conflict that critics say was a strategic misstep that is turning into a quagmire.

Last month, Trump said he views the Strait of Hormuz as “American territory”. Last week, he unilaterally renamed Lake Ontario, which borders both the US and Canada, as “Lake America” due to the ongoing US trade disagreements with Canada.

articles.title: Amazon drone delivery is coming to nearly 500 cities
articles.summary: Amazon Prime Air drone delivery plans to reach nearly 500 U.S. cities by the end of 2026, but your yard and ZIP code may determine eligibility.
articles.body: Amazon wants to make waiting for a package feel almost old-fashioned. Its Prime Air drone delivery service is gearing up for a major expansion, with plans to reach nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of 2026. For some shoppers, that could mean getting an eligible Amazon order dropped at home in as fast as 30 minutes. That is a huge jump from where things stand today. Amazon currently operates Prime Air from 11 U.S. locations across 10 metro areas, and the company says its drones have already delivered hundreds of thousands of packages this year. There is one detail worth keeping in mind when you hear that 500-city figure. Amazon is talking about communities served, rather than 500 individual drone hubs. Each Prime Air site can cover about 175 square miles, allowing one launch location to reach several nearby cities and towns. So, could one of these drones soon be heading toward your neighborhood? Here's where Prime Air is available now, what it costs and what you should know before choosing drone delivery at checkout. Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats , has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com DRONE DELIVERS 2 PIZZAS IN MINUTES Where Amazon drone delivery works today Prime Air currently serves the Phoenix, Tampa, Kansas City, Baton Rouge, Detroit, Omaha, Houston, Dallas, San Antonio and Waco metro areas. Those markets span seven states. Amazon says Chicago, Syracuse, Cleveland, Atlanta and Boise are next on its launch list. More communities are expected later this year. If you live in one of those metro areas, that still does not guarantee a drone will appear as a delivery choice. Amazon says coverage can vary by ZIP code and address. When your home qualifies, the drone option appears while you shop or at checkout. That is the easiest way to know whether Prime Air has reached you. You do not need a separate app or a special Amazon account. How fast can Amazon drone delivery reach your home? Amazon advertises Prime Air delivery in as fast as 30 minutes. However, the company says most drone orders currently arrive around 60 minutes after checkout. That could still save you a trip when you need something quickly. If you need a charger before a trip or medicine you would rather not drive out for, an hour can feel very different from waiting until tomorrow. Amazon says Prime Air can carry packages up to 5 pounds that fit roughly inside a large shoebox. The company says that makes more than 60% of the items customers buy most often eligible for drone delivery. The selection can include iPhones, Galaxy phones, AirPods, AirTags, Ring doorbells, groceries and household products. Of course, the exact selection depends on your location and what Amazon can safely load onto the drone. UFC STAR CONOR MCGREGOR GOES VIRAL FOR DRONE DELIVERY FIASCO AFTER UNDERGOING KNEE SURGERY What Amazon drone delivery costs What you pay for drone delivery depends on whether you have Prime and how much you order. Prime members pay no drone delivery fee when an eligible order totals $50 or more. Prime members pay $2.99 on smaller eligible orders. Customers without Prime pay $4.99. That pricing could make drone delivery tempting when you need something quickly. On the other hand, paying a fee to shave a few hours off a routine purchase may feel unnecessary. The bigger question may be how quickly you begin treating one-hour delivery as normal once it becomes available. How a Prime Air delivery reaches your yard If Prime Air is available at your address, you will see the drone delivery option when you check out on Amazon. For your first order, you choose a delivery spot on your property. You can use that same spot again or change it later. When the drone arrives, it checks the area before releasing your package. Amazon says it looks for people, pets, vehicles and other obstacles that could get in the way. That also means your yard could determine whether drone delivery works for you. Trees, landscaping or a pool may make it harder for the drone to find a safe place to drop your order. As Prime Air expands into more neighborhoods, Amazon will have to make sure each delivery spot gives the drone enough room to do its job safely. What about safety, privacy and noise? Amazon holds FAA Part 135 certification for Prime Air, the federal framework used for commercial drone package delivery. The FAA says Part 135 certification provides the path for operators carrying someone else's property for compensation beyond visual line of sight. Prime Air also uses a Detect-and-Avoid system. Amazon says the drone continuously scans the airspace around it and makes real-time decisions to avoid obstacles while flying. Then there is the privacy question. Prime Air drones use onboard cameras and sensors for navigation. Amazon says the drones do not track individuals or record their movements. The company also says no person watches a live camera feed, because the drone processes the camera data onboard for navigation. Noise may be the more noticeable issue for many neighborhoods. Amazon says the drone produces less sound during drop-off than an idling delivery truck parked at the curb. At cruising altitude, the company compares the sound with a window fan on low. Still, community complaints about drone noise have followed delivery programs before. As Amazon expands, local reaction could shape how smoothly Prime Air enters some neighborhoods. Why the 500-city goal will be a major test Amazon first showed off the idea of 30-minute drone delivery more than a decade ago. Since then, engineers have redesigned the aircraft while Amazon worked through aviation rules and local concerns. Now the company believes it has a version that can scale. Amazon CEO Andy Jassy told shareholders this year that Prime Air expects to reach communities with about 30 million customers by year-end. He also said the company plans to deliver half a billion packages by the end of the decade. Even with that ambition, drones will handle only a small slice of Amazon's overall deliveries for now. A drone carries one lightweight package at a time, while vans and trucks can move much larger loads. Amazon also has plenty of competition. Walmart and Alphabet-owned Wing plan to expand drone delivery to more than 270 Walmart stores by 2027. Meanwhile, DoorDash has received FAA Part 135 certification for its own drone operation. The race has moved beyond proving that a drone can carry a package. Companies now have to show that people will use the service regularly and that neighborhoods will accept more aircraft overhead. What this means to you For most people, the first sign that Prime Air has reached their area will be simple: a drone delivery option shows up at checkout. If you need something quickly, that could be genuinely useful. A forgotten charger, medicine or another small item could arrive before you would normally make it to the store and back. There are some limits to keep in mind. Your order has to fit Amazon's size and weight rules, your property needs a safe drop spot and bad weather can delay a flight. You may also have to decide how much speed is worth to you. More drone deliveries could mean more noise overhead and more questions about how these aircraft fit into everyday neighborhoods. If Prime Air becomes available at your address, I would try it when you actually need something fast. That is probably the best way to find out whether 30-minute delivery feels genuinely useful in your day-to-day life. FIREWORKS ARE FADING, BUT THEIR HIGH-TECH REPLACEMENT COMES WITH NEW RISKS Kurt's key takeaways Amazon has been chasing 30-minute drone delivery since Jeff Bezos introduced the idea in 2013. For years, it felt like a technology that was always coming soon. The scale of this new plan changes that conversation. I do not expect delivery vans to disappear. A 5-pound payload, changing weather, tricky yards and local rules give ground delivery plenty of work to do. But when you need a small item quickly, getting it in 30 to 60 minutes could become genuinely useful. What catches my attention most is how fast expectations can change. Same-day delivery once sounded incredibly fast. Now Amazon wants you thinking about whether an hour feels too long. Would you welcome Amazon drones over your neighborhood if they could get an order to your home in under an hour, or would you rather keep those deliveries on the road? articles.title: DHS condemns Rosie O’Donnell after ‘disgusting’ claim that detained immigrants are raped in ICE facilities
articles.summary: Rosie O'Donnell claimed ICE facilities are "concentration camps" where children are raped, prompting DHS to call her smears categorically false.
articles.body: The Department of Homeland Security condemned comedian Rosie O’Donnell and set the record straight after she made multiple wild claims about ICE facilities. In a TikTok titled, "Friday Ramble," O'Donnell discussed a variety of topics, including the recent death of country music legend Dolly Parton, before launching into criticism of the Trump administration. "We all vowed ‘Never Again,’ remember?" she said in the TikTok video, referencing the Holocaust. She noted that people even today are shocked at how Germans allowed fascism to take over before claiming fascism is in full swing in the United States. We’re raping children in detention, in ICE detention. They’re all getting pregnant," she said. "And they’re separated, males and females. Who has access to those girls? What happens to their babies? What do they do with them? There are big questions." While some public figures, like Joe Concha and the White House, have already blasted O’Donnell for her comments, a spokesman for the DHS rejected her claims in comments to Fox News Digital. "These disgusting, reckless and categorically FALSE smears are directly contributing to our officers facing a 1,300% increase in assaults, a 3,300% increase in vehicular attacks and an 8,000% increase in death threats against them," the spokesman for the DHS said in an exclusive statement. "Moreover, comparisons of illegal alien detention centers to internment camps used during World War II are deranged and lazy. "These celebrities remain quiet about the humanitarian crisis that was manufactured by the Biden administration’s open border policies and the several hundred thousand children exploited, trafficked and missing on their watch," the spokesman added. "Under President Trump, ICE is dedicated to locating these unaccompanied children that came in through the border under Biden. Sadly, the extremely unstable, TDS-suffering lunatic Rosie O’Donnell — who fled the country in protest of President Trump’s historic, landslide re-election — would rather spin fake news that benefits the traffickers, smugglers and rapists than acknowledge the nightmare so many children lived under Democrat control. "Our agents are focused on protecting the American people — not entertaining performative outrage. Where is the outrage for angel families who lost a loved one to illegal alien crime?" the spokesman asked. "To most Americans, our brave ICE law enforcement are heroes. Eighty percent of Americans support arresting and deporting criminal illegal aliens from American neighborhoods. These officers put their lives on the line every day to arrest the worst of the worst, including murderers, pedophiles, rapists, gang members and terrorists. ANGEL DAD TAKES MAJOR NEW ROLE AFTER DAUGHTER’S KILLING SPARKS SWEEPING ILLEGAL ALIEN CRACKDOWN "ICE has authority for lawful arrests where authorized under 8 USC 1357. Law enforcement officers use ‘reasonable suspicion’ to investigate immigration status and probable cause to make arrests consistent with the statute and the Fourth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. The Supreme Court has already vindicated us on these practices," the spokesman added. The department disputed O'Donnell's claims about conditions at ICE facilities. "Claims that there are subprime conditions at ICE detention centers are FALSE. ICE has higher detention standards than most U.S. prisons that hold actual U.S. citizens," the DHS spokesman added in the statement. "All detainees are provided with three meals a day, clean water, clothing, bedding, showers, soap and toiletries. Illegal aliens also have access to phones to communicate with their family members and lawyers. Certified dieticians evaluate meals. In fact, ICE has higher detention standards than most U.S. prisons that hold actual U.S. citizens. "It is a longstanding practice to provide comprehensive medical care from the moment an alien enters ICE custody. This includes medical, dental and mental health services as available and access to medical appointments and 24-hour emergency care. For many illegal aliens, this is the best healthcare they have received their entire lives," he added. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE The department also pushed back against the actress's claims about pregnant detainees. "Pregnancy in ICE detention is exceedingly rare, making up 0.15% of all illegal aliens currently in custody, as of June 30," the DHS spokesman said. "Pregnant women receive regular prenatal visits, mental health services, nutritional support and accommodations aligned with community standards of care. In addition to medical, mental health and dental services provided to all detained women as required by ICE detention standards, facilities provide women with pregnancy services such as pregnancy testing, routine or specialized prenatal care, postpartum follow-up and nursing services." O'Donnell has a long history of blasting the Trump administration, particularly ICE enforcement. In July 2025, she made similar comparisons between ICE and Nazi Germany, saying, "I think Americans should stand up and say, ‘No way. You’re not going to silence us. You don’t have the right to silence us. You never did. And you never will. We, the people, have the right to speak up against atrocities which are happening on a daily basis.’ ICE, his own personal Gestapo — what will it take, America? What will it take? CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "He’s going to arrest every artist that disagrees with him, and pretty much every artist does," she said. "Whether or not they’re brave enough to say it is another thing." "Being in detention is a choice," the DHS spokesman said. "We encourage all illegal aliens to take control of their departure with the CBP Home App. The United States is offering illegal aliens $3,000 and a free flight to self-deport now. We encourage every person here illegally to take advantage of this offer and reserve the chance to come back to the U.S. the right legal way to live the American dream. If not, you will be arrested and deported without a chance to return." "Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, ICE is targeting the worst of the worst," the spokesman concluded. "Nearly 70% of ICE arrests are of illegal aliens charged or convicted of a crime in the U.S. Our message is clear: If you come into our country illegally and break our laws, we will find you wherever you are, we will arrest you and we will deport you." A clip posted by @Dirk_mp4 shows White looking at photos of Morgpie and giving his blunt opinion about how she looks. He said some of her appearances looked “too masculine” and added, “Like this one easily could be a Trans...” His comments have become the main point of the latest controversy around the streamer. The situation is also tied to older comments and criticism surrounding Morgpie. She is a Twitch streamer, cosplayer and fitness creator with around 420,000 Twitch followers. Her online career has included several controversial Twitch moments, while Nick White has previously criticized her content for being too sexual for a platform where children could potentially see it. Separate claims from another streamer, Nick Lee, have also circulated, adding more fuel to the rumors.What Nick White said about Morgpie’s appearanceThe latest controversy comes from a clip where Nick White reacts to different pictures of Morgpie. He also said that one of the looks “easily could be a Trans” and connected his opinion to whether he found the appearance attractive.That is the direct basis of the current controversy. articles.title: Is Texas accepting gold, silver as payment from September 1? Here's what you need to know
articles.summary: US News: A new law that allows Texas to begin implementing th eframework to accept certain gold and silver as legal tender came to effect on September 1 but th.
articles.body: A new law that allows Texas to begin implementing th eframework to accept certain gold and silver as legal tender came to effect on September 1 but that does not mean gold and silver have already become legal tender in the state.House Bill 1056, authored by Republican state Rep Mark Dorazio of San Antonio, recognizes qualifying privately produced gold and silver specie as legal tender in Texas beginning Sept. 1. The metal must be marked with its weight and purity and cannot bear markings suggesting that it was issued by a government. No person, business or government agency will be required to accept it.“I spent forty years building a construction company,” said Dorazio. “I’ve watched inflation eat the paychecks and the savings of the people who build this country. The problem isn’t only that things cost more — it’s that the dollar buys less every year.” Dorazio said that although no one is required to use it, the new law provides Texans “a way to protect what they’ve earned.”“How am I supposed to buy groceries or put gas in my car with a gold bar?” Dorazio asked during a legislative hearing. “Fortunately, the technology is available today and allows you to pay for goods and services using a gold card through the convenience of a debit card.”According to the law, the comptroller’s office will contract with a debit card provider, which will facilitate the conversion of gold and silver deposited into an account to dollar amounts at the point of sale. That electronic-payment component, however, does not begin Sept. 1. The provisions authorizing systems backed by bullion held in the Texas Bullion Depository take effect May 1, 2027, and implementation will depend on action by the state comptroller, local reports said.Before Texas, Florida officially recognized gold and silver coins as legal tender starting July 1.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Tens of thousands rally in Spain in support of Ceuta, against Sánchez
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of people have rallied across Spain in support of the North African exclave of Ceuta's place within Spain and against the Madrid government...
articles.body:
Tens of thousands rally across Spain in support of Ceuta and against the Madrid government's migration policy.

Participants accuse Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez of pursuing an appeasement policy towards Morocco and failing to provide adequate support to Ceuta.

Ceuta faced an influx of 72,000 migrants in two days, with around 5,000 still in the territory a month later, leading to ongoing protests and challenges for the region.

Tens of thousands of people have rallied across Spain in support of the North African exclave of Ceuta's place within Spain and against the Madrid government's migration policy, amid an ongoing migration crisis in the territory.

Participants and speakers accused Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's central government on Wednesday of pursuing an appeasement policy towards Morocco and of failing to provide adequate support to Ceuta.

While Morocco has long claimed Ceuta - as it has the other North African Spanish exclave of Melilla - it is not currently applying any particular pressure on the issue.

Spanish opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, of the conservative People's Party, nonetheless spoke of an "invasion" by migrants backed by Morocco. He accused Sánchez and his government of lying, saying they had claimed there had been no warning of the migration crisis and that Morocco had not instigated it. Both claims were untrue, he said.

In Ceuta, thousands of people gathered beneath a sea of Spanish flags, demanding a return to normality and calling for the enclave to remain part of Spain. "Ceuta does not sell out, Ceuta does not surrender," read banners at the rally.

According to government figures, at least 72,000 migrants entered Ceuta on July 30 and 31. A month later, around 5,000 of them were still in the exclave, some camping on streets and beaches - a situation that has placed a heavy burden on the territory's 83,000 residents.

Protests have continued to take place, and there have been repeated violent attacks on migrants and private aid organizations.

Spain is legally barred from carrying out collective deportations and must rule on each asylum application individually, a process that could take weeks or months.

The Spanish central government has also ruled out transferring the migrants to the mainland, because Ceuta is not part of the Schengen Area and other Schengen members could then introduce border checks with Spain - as Italy has already done.

The rallies on Ceuta's regional holiday were called by FEMP, the umbrella body representing Spanish municipalities, which is led by the People's Party. The far-right populist Vox party also took part in the demonstrations.

"Ceuta is Spanish and will not be abandoned," said Mayor José Luis Martínez-Almeida.

According to the central government's representative, around 50,000 people attended the rally in Madrid, which the national broadcaster RTVE said was the largest single event of the evening.

People's Party Secretary General Miguel Tellado said around 2,000 rallies had taken place across Spain and again called for the government to resign and for fresh elections to be held.

In some cities, including Barcelona and Bilbao, counter-demonstrations were held at which participants spoke out against racism. "No human being is illegal," read banners at those events
